`lane/wf-violation-exact @ cdb4c66c` and `lane/meals-violation-exact @ 13cd9f18`, both unpushed, both
container-free green at their own bases.

**Why this is worth landing as one lane rather than two merges:** the modules are independent, so the
merge should be additive — but the *claim* is not per-module. "This estate does not mistake a NOT NULL
failure for a uniqueness clash" is either true or it is not, and it is false while either half is out.

**What the Meals half discovered is the reason it matters.** The pinned production write is the funding
bind — the single point at which an order becomes company-funded. Under the loose predicate a NOT NULL
fault there answered `MEALS_RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND`: **checkout is told a live reservation vanished, the

**One thing the merge must not "tidy".** `IsDeterministicConstraintViolation` in the Meals file **keeps
the bare 19 deliberately** — that predicate wants the whole family for poison quarantine, and narrowing
it would be the opposite bug. A reviewer seeing 19 survive in the same file must read the comment, not
the diff.

Seven merge lanes have run: build the merge before any tier, read auto-merged bodies rather than trusting
a zero conflict count, diff the discovered-test sets, resolve `artifacts/tests/README.md` as a union, and
move the ref only with `git update-ref <ref> <new> <old>`.


### Lane L-WORKTREE-BASENAME-PIN — a test stops failing for every lane that follows the rules
state: verified
class: node
pts: 1

agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-WORKTREE-BASENAME-PIN/evidence.md

**Reported by seven lanes as "pre-existing, not chased". The seventh measured what it actually costs.**

`test/journey-artifact-store.test.js:457` asserts the build id matches `/^Web-modules@…/` — the checkout's
**directory name**. Every lane in this program is required to work in **its own worktree**, and a worktree
is never named `Web-modules`.

**So the rule the estate enforces guarantees this test reds for every lane that follows it.** Not
occasionally: always, for all of them, permanently.

The cost is not the red. It is that **every lane must now carry a sentence explaining which red is
allowed** — and a suite with a standing permitted failure is a suite where the next real red gets
explained away by the same reflex. This estate has already paid for that shape twice: a flake nobody
could name because it was re-run until green, and a tree that is always dirty so nobody notices when it
is dirty for a reason.

It belongs to the lane that introduced the identity concept, and every lane that hit it correctly
declined to chase it into somebody else's file. **Seven declines is where deferring stops being courtesy.**

The fix is small: assert the identity the artifact is *for* — the repository, resolved from git rather
than from the directory name — or pin the directory only when it is the canonical checkout.

**Second item, same class, from the same lane:** `test/e2e/fixture/meals.js` has drifted from the model.
Neither the invitation model nor the claim response carries `employeeReference`, so the guest-claim
journey **can only ever render the fallback** — and its assertion is `not.toBe('—')`, which cannot separate
the branches anyway. The lane fixed the false comment and **deliberately left the fixture and the
assertion**, because it could not run Playwright and *a pin it did not watch fail is not a pin*. That
judgement was right; the drift is still real.


### Lane L-PUSH-TOKEN-IN-PATH — a device push token stops travelling in a URL
state: verified
class: suite
pts: 3
exit: neither notification registration route carries a device push token in its path, the token is absent from request telemetry for an authenticated caller, and the four Core clients call the new shape, pinned by a route-shape row that reds if a credential-named parameter returns, recorded in ../OkamAPI-modules/lanes/L-PUSH-TOKEN-IN-PATH/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: ../OkamAPI-modules/lanes/L-PUSH-TOKEN-IN-PATH/mutation-log.md

**Found by `L-ROUTE-GUARD-GAPS` while building the credential-name census it was asked to consider, and
it is worse than the brief that sent it supposed. I verified the shape myself at the tip:**

```
Controllers/ConsumerNotificationController.cs:11  [Authorize]
Controllers/ConsumerNotificationController.cs:31  [HttpGet("{handle}")]
```

**`{handle}` is the APNS/FCM device push token**, handed straight to `GetRegistrationsByChannelAsync`.
The same shape exists on `StoreNotificationController`.

**It is a credential, and it is in a GET path.** A push token is what lets a holder send notifications to
that device. A URL is seen by every intermediary, every reverse proxy and every access log — and this
plan has already ruled that **redaction at one sink is not a fix for an identifier in a path.**

**And here there is no redaction at any sink.** Both routes are `[Authorize]`d, so they miss **both**
telemetry triggers — one fires only on anonymous endpoints with guid-shaped values, the other is itself a
name rule that does not know this name. **The token is published in the clear on the wire and unredacted
into Application Insights.**

C7's `holds_because` is exactly this: Application Insights retains what is written to it, so a credential
logged at any level is published to everyone with portal access and to history nobody can edit. **The
estate has paid that bill twice — the Wolt callback signing secret and a live refresh token — and both
times the rotation cost far more than the code fix.** A device token cannot be rotated by us at all; only
the device re-registering replaces it.

**Why it was recorded rather than closed, and rightly:** the fix is a verb-and-body change to a route
**four client apps call through Core's notification service**, so it is a contract change across repos,
not an edit. The lane recorded it as an **open gap with a reason** and refused to allowlist it as
deliberate — which is the correct handling of something you have found and cannot safely fix in place.

C3 applies to the fix: the route, the Core client and the four callers move in the same change, or the
capability breaks.


### Lane L-MEALS-AGREEMENT-PIN-INVERTS — a test stops asserting the defect it was written beside
state: verified
class: suite
pts: 2
exit: MealsAgreementWriterTests asserts that a refused agreement write replays its refusal rather than that it strands its key, and the one-active-corridor stranding site records a refusal, pinned by a test that reds if either goes back, recorded in lanes/L-MEALS-AGREEMENT-PIN-INVERTS/mutation-log.md, recorded in lanes/L-MEALS-AGREEMENT-PIN-INVERTS/adoption-review.md
agent: meals-pin
needs: D-SPEC-L-MEALS-AGREEMENT-PIN-INVERTS
evidence: lanes/L-MEALS-AGREEMENT-PIN-INVERTS/adoption-review.md

**Held on its own D-SPEC, written here rather than kept by the clerk.** This lane returned `fail-spec`:
both briefed halves were **already built at `54714dd6`**. Re-dispatching sends a second agent to
rediscover that, which is the wall this program has walked into before.

What remains genuinely open is narrower than the lane's title and is on the decision: a pin for the
exit's third clause, which its mutant M3 showed was real — **blank the recorded refusal's detail and the
existing assertions all still pass, so a retry that re-decides and a retry that replays are
indistinguishable to that test.** The lane built it at `4bbf34a5` and offered it **take-or-drop rather
than claiming `built`**, which is why it is Sven's call and not mine.


**Found by `L-MEALS-IDEMPOTENCY-REFUSAL` when its own fix turned a green suite red — which is the only
way this kind of thing surfaces.**

`MealsAgreementWriterTests` does not merely describe the stranding defect. **It asserts it**: receipt
`CompletedAtUtc` null, retry answers in-progress — under a comment calling it *"the module's documented
stuck-reservation tradeoff"*.

**A test pinning a defect as intended behaviour is not neutral. It is a standing instruction to keep the
defect**, and it is stronger than a comment, because the next person to fix the code meets a red suite and
concludes they broke something. That is what happened here, in the mildest possible form — the lane read
it, recognised it, and reported it rather than deleting the assertion to get green.

**This estate has now met the same shape three times**: a wire test pinning a credit note's wrong
filename, a SQL-tier test asserting that a retry needs a fresh key, and this one. Each was written
honestly against the behaviour of its day; each became an instruction the moment the behaviour was
supposed to change.

**Second item, from the same lane and not in anyone's list before it:** the **one-active-corridor check**
is a stranding site the earlier enumeration missed. So any comment or document that enumerates the
stranding sites is now **incomplete as well as stale** — `L-MEALS-DOCSYNC` has been told.

Do not simply delete the assertion. **Invert it**, so the suite pins the behaviour the module now
promises, and keep the original wording in the test's history rather than erasing that it was once true.


**Ruled `adopt-the-offered-pin` on 2026-08-05.** **The exit below asks this lane to build what already exists on a branch.** Adopt it instead, through a dedicated review: one commit off its base, **its only production hunk is a comment correction** both lanes would otherwise have dropped, and its test lines pin the clause that was genuinely open — a retry that re-decides being indistinguishable from one that replays. **The reviewer supplies the assertion the lane declined to assert**; that is what cures the single objection.


**Reviewed and adopted 2026-08-05 — and the reviewer supplied the assertion the offering lane withheld, then
found that lane's own stated proof wrong.**

**It built a mutant nobody had run**: a refused receipt reopened and told to proceed, so the retry genuinely
**re-decides** instead of replaying. The new assertion goes **red** under it — no exception thrown, the
re-decide reaching the moved world and signing the corridor — while the older one **survives**, including the
message-equality line the commit added. **The pin discriminates.**

**But the mutation log credits the wrong mutant.** The one it names is a *replay* mutant, and a re-decided
refusal is produced by the same deterministic check carrying the same message. **Only the moved world
separates the two**, and the adopted commit is the only place at this site that moves it.

**A correction to the ruling's framing: the clause was not globally open.** The same mutant also reds eight
pre-existing backstop tests and two receipt-level ones, all already landed — they get the discriminator free,
because their arranged fault reaches only the first call. **It was open for one family**, which is exactly the
site the exit names.

**Routing condition, verified by the clerk rather than relayed:** none of the three commits is an ancestor of
the backend tip, and `lane/replay-pins-close` **carries all of them plus the tip**. So the commit **cannot be
taken alone**, and if that branch is the integration route, separate adoption **duplicates merged work**.

**Matrix: five mutants killed, no survivors, baseline and restore both clean**, and the comment hunk verified
against the tip — the stale text is there verbatim and both of its factual claims hold.

**Disclosed rather than hidden, and it is the second instance today:** a first baseline omitted the SQL
exclusion from its filter and **started a container the lane had no slot for.** The harness reaped it, nothing
foreign was touched, and the clerk confirmed zero containers running afterwards. **No SQL tier was measured
and none is claimed. C5 is owed** — nobody has walked this in a UI.

### Lane L-XZ-PRINTED-DEFECTS — the printed fiscal document stops omitting and mislabelling
state: verified
class: suite
pts: 2
exit: the delivery-receipt count appears on the printed X and Z, no payment label falls back to an enum identifier, and the received sum excludes the receivable, pinned by a rendered-document test that reds if any of the three returns, recorded in lanes/L-XZ-PRINTED-DEFECTS/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-XZ-PRINTED-DEFECTS/mutation-log.md

**Three defects `L-XZ-CREDIT-FIELDS` found while building, all on the printed statutory document —
kassasystemforskrifta artifacts an inspector reads.**

1. **`Row` truncated `Utleveringskvitteringer (1)`** to the amount alone — so **a § 2-8-2 count was stated
   nowhere on the document.** Not wrong, absent: the reader cannot tell a missing count from a zero.
2. **`PaymentLabel` fell back to the enum identifier**, so a Norwegian fiscal document would print
   `CompanyAccount`. A statutory document in the wrong language is not a cosmetic defect; it is a
   document an inspector cannot read as the record it claims to be.
3. **`Sum mottatt` absorbed the receivable** — money not received counted as received.

C6 governs: a statutory claim is printed only where the document it claims can be produced. **These are
the document.** Do not widen the statutory naming and do not add a § reference while in there.

Pin on the **rendered** document, not the model — all three defects live in rendering, and a model-level
assertion would have passed on every one of them.


### Lane L-MEALS-MEMBERS-READ — the enrolled set can be read back, not only written
state: built-unverified
class: suite
pts: 2
exit: a programme's enrolled members are readable by identity so the admin surface can pre-tick them, and a claimed-but-unenrolled member's ineligibility carries a reason code, pinned by a test per half that reds if either returns to silence, recorded in lanes/L-MEALS-MEMBERS-READ/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-MEALS-MEMBERS-READ/mutation-log.md

**Two backend gaps `L-MEALS-ENROL-UI` hit while wiring the surface. It could not close either, said so,
and built the UI to state the gap rather than paper over it — which is why they are legible at all.**

**1. Nothing reads the enrolled set back.** A programme carries a **count**; only the write's own response
names identities. So the admin panel cannot pre-tick who is already enrolled, and the lane deliberately
left it unticked with the reason on screen: **a guess would silently un-enrol whoever it guessed wrong
about.** That is the correct call and it is not a fix — `GET /programs/{id}/members` is.

**2. A claimed-but-unenrolled member reads `eligible:false` with no reason code at all.**
`MealsQuoteService.cs:426` sets one only for *revoked* or *enrolled-outside-window*. **This is the dead end
the employee was actually sitting in** — the surface can tell them they are not eligible and cannot tell
them why, or what would change it.

Both halves are the same defect wearing different clothes: **a read that answers with less than the caller
needs to act.** A count without identities, and a refusal without a cause.

The reason-code half touches the quote path — **Meals is a money path**, so if the change reaches a write
rather than a read, C4 applies and the actor is named and asserted by value.

### Lane L-REPLAY-PINS-RECHECK — the other two replay pins are checked for the hole Training found
state: verified
class: suite
pts: 2
exit: the Workforce and Meals same-key retry tests are shown to distinguish a replayed refusal from a re-decided one, or the gap is named per test with the world change that would close it, recorded in lanes/L-REPLAY-PINS-RECHECK/census.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-REPLAY-PINS-RECHECK/census.md

**`L-TRAIN-IDEMPOTENCY-REFUSAL` found a hole in its own pin that neither sibling record carries, and it
applies to work already merged.**

Its mutant M04 — deleting the replay rethrow — came back **green**. The reason is the finding:
**without the rethrow, a `Refused` reservation re-executes the staging callback — and with the world
unchanged it refuses again with the identical code.** All 22 assertions passed **for the wrong reason**.

**Same-code-on-retry does not prove a replay.** It proves the second call reached the same conclusion,
which is exactly what a *working* replay and a *broken* one both look like from outside.

It closed the hole by **repairing the refusal's precondition between the two calls and counting rows** —
so a re-decide would now succeed and a replay must still refuse. That is the discriminator, and it is
cheap.

**Three lanes built this primitive and only the third looked for this.** `L-WF-IDEMPOTENCY-REFUSAL`,
`L-WF-IDEMPOTENCY-REFUSAL-REST` and `L-MEALS-IDEMPOTENCY-REFUSAL` all assert `code` out of the body on a
same-key retry. **Read each and rule whether it discriminates** — and note a sibling has already shown one
does not: `L-MEALS-AGREEMENT-PIN-INVERTS` proved that blanking a recorded refusal's detail leaves the
existing code-and-status assertions passing.

**This is not a criticism of those lanes.** Each was careful, each mutation-proved its own change, and the
hole is invisible until you ask what the *other* branch would have answered. That is why it is worth one
lane to ask across all three rather than trusting three independent greens.

Where a pin does not discriminate, **name the world change that would close it** rather than rewriting the
test — the fix belongs with whoever owns the lane.

### Lane L-ROW-FIT-GOODS-GROUPS — the fit rule's remaining count-bearing rows are pinned at width
state: verified
class: suite
pts: 1
exit: every count-bearing printed row keeps its digits at the widths where the label must shorten, pinned by a width-swept test that reds if a trailing digit group becomes shortenable again, recorded in lanes/L-ROW-FIT-GOODS-GROUPS/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-ROW-FIT-GOODS-GROUPS/mutation-log.md

**A follow-on from `L-XZ-PRINTED-DEFECTS`, whose headline is the lesson: a fix measured against one world
is a fix for one world.**

A sibling reported the missing-count defect fixed. **It was not.** The fix shrank the label
(`Utleveringskvitteringer` to `Utleveringskvitt.`) and was measured against **a single world** — one-digit
count, ten-character amount, landing on exactly the 21 characters available — **and its guard test built
that same world.** Every count of ten or more re-truncated:

```
count 12    ->  'Utleveringskvitt. (1... 999 999,99'   twelve receipts read as one
count 1234  ->  'Utleveringskvitt. ... 1 234 567,89'   count absent
```

**The reported symptom was a count stated nowhere. What survived states a count that is wrong and
plausible — the worse failure, because a missing figure invites a question and a confident wrong one does
not.**

The fix landed at the **choke point**: a trailing all-digit group is excluded from what may be shortened,
so **the descriptive words give way and the figures never do**. That covers the goods-group and
per-operator rows too, which carried the same latent exposure.

This lane exists to keep it that way: **sweep the widths rather than picking one.** A pin built on a
single width is what let this through twice.


### Flag F-SPLICE-RESIDUE-IN-BRIEFS — the old splice damage is still generating garbled briefs
state: open
severity: warn
owner: @sven
clears_when: no lane block's prose runs into the next block's header on one line, and no dispatched brief contains a fragment of another lane
cleared_by: L-MEALS-PROJECTION-LAG-VISIBLE

**A lane was dispatched today with a brief whose middle seventy lines were fragments of two other lanes,
spliced mid-sentence, twice. It executed the legible exit and named the discrepancy rather than
improvising — which is the only reason this was found.**

The cause is the batch-edit splice earlier in this program: an edit applied by byte offset while mutating
the same string, which deleted 22 lane blocks. They were restored from a view generated before the
damage, and each says its prose is unrecoverable. **What nobody checked was the seams.** Thirteen blocks
had their prose cut **mid-word** with the next block's `state:` line running on directly:

```
...the rebuild control is elevated-role only — sstate: built-unverified
```

`plan check` reports **0 errors** on that, and did throughout. The parser recovers, the rendered views
recover — **and the brief generator does not**, because it copies the block body verbatim. So the damage
was invisible in every place anyone looked and visible only to an agent reading its own brief.

**Repaired structurally, not editorially.** I split each seam so the header starts its own line. **The
truncated prose is left truncated** — a sentence ending "…and the billin" stays that way, because
inventing the rest is exactly the failure this plan exists to prevent, and a lane reading a half-sentence
knows it is half. Thirteen lines split, line count reconciled.

**What is not fixed:** the missing prose itself, and whatever briefs were generated from the seams before
today. If a lane's brief looked strange in the last two days, this is why.


### Lane L-MEALS-ENROL-PRETICK — the enrolment panel pre-ticks who is already enrolled
state: verified
class: node
pts: 1
exit: the enrolment control arrives with existing members already ticked and the not-readable note gone, driven through the page by a test that reds if the read is ignored, recorded in lanes/L-MEALS-ENROL-PRETICK/evidence.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-MEALS-ENROL-PRETICK/evidence.md

**The backend gap that forced a deliberate compromise is closed, so the compromise can go.**

`L-MEALS-ENROL-UI` built the enrolment surface and **left it unticked on purpose**, with the reason on
screen: nothing read the enrolled set back, so **a guess would silently un-enrol whoever it guessed wrong
about.** That was the right call and it was never the fix.

`L-MEALS-MEMBERS-READ` built the read — `GET /v1/meals/programs/{programId}/members`, **`Enrolled` rows
only**, deliberately: a `Removed` row answered back would **re-tick somebody an admin had taken out**, which
is the same mistake in the other direction. It carries the programme revision, because the enrolment write
compare-and-swaps on it.

So this lane is small: consume the read, pre-tick, and **delete the note** — the note is a claim about the
product, and it stops being true the moment the read lands.

**Two things not to lose.** The write is a compare-and-swap on the revision the read returns, so **use the
revision from this read** rather than one held from elsewhere. And the sibling's mutation is the standard
to keep: **unbinding the control must red a test**, driven by clicking rather than by calling the handler —
a lane this session found a page test that asserted nothing because it called the handler directly.

**Do not pre-tick from the write's own response.** That is the shortcut that looks equivalent and is not:
it is right only immediately after a write, and wrong on every page load.


### Lane L-ACCOUNTING-EXPORT-SILENT — an export that ran on nothing stops reporting that it ran
state: verified
class: suite
pts: 2
exit: an accounting export with no providers registered reports that it exported nothing rather than a store count, and the same is true of the capture sweep, pinned by a test per site that reds if the empty case is reported as success, recorded in lanes/L-ACCOUNTING-EXPORT-SILENT/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-ACCOUNTING-EXPORT-SILENT/mutation-log.md

**The sharpest of four silent sites `L-DI-COLLECTION-SILENT` found, and it is on the books.**

`AccountingExportOrchestrator` takes its providers as a collection. **With none registered it returns an
empty result — and `MaintenanceService.cs:160` still sets `StoresExported = N` from a different database
query.** So the books go unexported while **the job, the operator route and the result object all say the
export ran.**

The count is not wrong about anything it measured; it measured **the wrong thing**. It counts stores that
*should* have been exported, from a query that never consults whether a provider existed to export them.

**Second site, same shape:** `MaintenanceService.captureSweepers` — an empty collection yields a clean
`PaymentCaptureSweepResult` while **every reservation expires uncaptured**. Worse, `Array.Empty` is the
**test default**, so the suite's ordinary case is the broken one.

**Both are money.** This is the report-success-you-did-not-achieve family that this plan has already
removed from a push adapter and a delivery record — and here it is on the accounting export, where the
consequence is books that nobody knows are missing.

Sven's standing ruling applies: **withhold rather than zero.** A count that cannot be established must say
so; a number that means "we did not check" must not be printed as though it means "none".

**Do not fix by adding a floor alone.** A floor on provider count stops the empty case but leaves the
count still measuring the wrong thing — the result must report what was *exported*, not what was
*eligible*.

### Lane L-TELEMETRY-INITIALIZER-FLOOR — the redaction that C7 depends on cannot silently be absent
state: built-unverified
class: suite
pts: 2
exit: an empty telemetry-initializer collection is refused at composition rather than accepted, pinned by a test that reds if the registration is removed, recorded in lanes/L-TELEMETRY-INITIALIZER-FLOOR/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-TELEMETRY-INITIALIZER-FLOOR/mutation-log.md

**`ITelemetryInitializer` is collection-shaped and unchecked — so an empty sequence puts capability tokens
into Application Insights. C7 by omission.**

Named by `L-DI-COLLECTION-SILENT`, and it is the twin of a defect closed hours earlier: a device push
token travelled in a URL path and **missed both telemetry triggers**, publishing a credential in the
clear and unredacted. That was fixed by moving the token. **This is the other half — the redaction itself
can simply not be there, and nothing says so.**

C7's `holds_because` is exactly this: **App Insights retains what is written to it**, so a credential
logged at any level is published to everyone with portal access and to history nobody can edit. The
estate has paid that bill twice, and both times the rotation cost far more than the code fix.

**A guard on registration count is the right shape here**, unlike the accounting site — the initializers
are a set that must be present, not a computation whose result must be honest. But **assert the specific
initializers by type**, not merely that the sequence is non-empty: one unrelated initializer present would
satisfy a count and redact nothing.

The census also names `IHostedService` ×10 with the same exposure — deleting `AddHostedService` is
invisible, and **4 of the 10, including both money loops, fall outside the reachability sweep's namespace
scope.** That is a third lane; name it in the return rather than absorbing it.

`lane/ev-outbox-flake @ 59a1d607` and `lane/ev-outbox-guid-substring @ 79f9dd7d` are **neither an ancestor

200,000-body sampling of 1 in 197.6 — two methods agreeing is what makes the number usable.

**It also corrected both earlier figures as optimistic**, and named why: `22/16^3` is an **expected count,

### Lane L-FRAGILE-NEEDLES — three assertions that pass only because their haystack is empty today
state: verified
class: suite
pts: 1
exit: no absence assertion depends on a field being unpopulated, each of the three named sites either excises its haystack or pins the emptiness it relies on, recorded in lanes/L-FRAGILE-NEEDLES/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-FRAGILE-NEEDLES/mutation-log.md

**A fourth site, found by `L-ROW-FIT-GOODS-GROUPS` and different in kind: a comment that cites an example
its own code cannot produce.** The choke-point fit guard justifies itself with `"Kort (Stripe)"` and
`"Vipps (Dintero)"` as labels that must still shorten as prose — **but those never reach the row builder in
that form**, because the payment label always has a rendered count appended first. **The guard is right;
its stated reason is not an example the builder can make.** That is a comment asserting a fact the code
falsifies, which this program has now removed from four other places — and it is worth the same treatment:
cite an example the code can actually produce, or say the guard is for a label that does not exist yet.

**Not aliasing — the mirror of it, and `L-ALIASING-NEEDLE-SWEEP` flagged these as comment-worthy rather
than fixing them. They are worth a small lane because each is one field away from permanent red.**

`GrowthErasureRefCountTests.cs:130` searches for **`"8"` — a single character.** It passes only because
the deferred erasure receipt writes a null destroyer and a null timestamp, so the haystack **holds no
digits at all.** Add one count or one timestamp and it is red forever, for a reason having nothing to do
with what it asserts.

The same shape covers the **one-to-two character `StoreId` needles** in the two tenant sweeps.

**These are the inverse of the aliasing family.** Those fail at random because the haystack contains
something; these pass reliably because it contains nothing — **and both are assertions whose truth rests
on a property nobody declared.** The remedy is the same: excise the haystack, or pin the emptiness the
assertion depends on so that changing it fails loudly and locally rather than mysteriously and later.

The sweep also found **a new form nobody had matched: the needle itself being the random part** — a
six-digit generated code searched in a log line, quantified at 1 in 1.51M. Safe, and on the record with
its number, which is the standard this census set.


### Flag F-TWO-FINALIZE-CONTROLS — two surfaces bind one irreversible freeze
state: open
severity: warn
owner: @sven
clears_when: exactly one surface binds the finalize endpoints, and the refusal it renders names the exception blocking it
cleared_by: L-MEALS-RECONCILE-UI

**Caught live, by a lane watching the shared checkout go dirty underneath it rather than by a merge.**

`L-MEALS-RECONCILE-UI` and `L-MEALS-STATEMENT-SURFACE` **both bind the finalize endpoints.** The second
was adding `/admin/meals-statements` to the navigation while the first was finishing.

**A freeze is irreversible, and two controls for it is worse than either alone** — an operator who finds
the wrong one gets a refusal that does not say what blocks it. In the lane's own words: *"the merge must
decide which surface owns the finalize, or you ship two controls for one irreversible freeze and only one
names its blocker."*

**Only one of them names the blocker, and that took real work.** The wire contract carries
`openExceptionCount` and **no id, kind, source key or company**, so naming what blocks a finalize needed a
**join** of the refusal against the queue read — **scoped to the billed company**, because the guard
counts per `(store, company)` while the queue answers for the whole venue. That lane also declined to port
an existing branch's banner that renders a count and names nothing.

**This did not wait for the merge because I told the running lane.** It can consume what exists, or argue
its surface should own the finalize and say what happens to the other control — either is fine; silently
binding it twice is not.

**The general shape, and it is new in this program:** every collision recorded so far was found *at* a
merge or by a reviewer reading two branches. This one was found by a lane **noticing a shared file change
under it while it worked** — which is the only place a two-controls-for-one-write conflict is cheap to
fix.


### Lane L-REPLAY-PINS-CLOSE — the four non-discriminating retry tests get the world change that closes them
state: verified
class: suite
pts: 2
exit: each of the four named same-key retry tests fails when the retry re-decides instead of replaying, pinned by the world change the census specified, recorded in lanes/L-REPLAY-PINS-CLOSE/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-REPLAY-PINS-CLOSE/mutation-log.md

**`L-REPLAY-PINS-RECHECK` enumerated 36 same-key-retry candidates across nine files and ruled each by
reading, asking one question: *if the retry had re-executed instead of replaying, would this test still
pass?* Four answer yes. The census names the world change for each.**

- `WorkforceShiftExchangeTests.cs:250` — the role link is deleted before **both** calls and never restored,
  so a re-decide refuses identically.
- `WorkforceShiftExchangeTests.cs:284` — **its comment claims only the recorded outcome can answer the
  retry, and that is false.** The competing-award interceptor has no INSERT/UPDATE filter, so it fires on a
  **read** outside any transaction and the competing row **survives** — proven by a sibling test's own green
  row count. The revalidation never checks already-awarded, so a re-decide re-hits the index with the
  identical code **and** aggregate id.
- `MealsIdempotencyRefusalTests.cs:311` — the only Meals test with **no arranged fault**, hence the only one
  whose world does not change by itself, and no row assertion either.
- `MealsAgreementWriterTests.cs:173` — its `1 agreement / 0 audit` assertions **look** like the discriminator
  and hold under a re-decide too. A second independent blind spot at a site another lane had already flagged.

**The structural finding is the one to carry.** Training's surviving mutant has **no literal counterpart**
in Workforce or Meals: both throw the replayed refusal from inside the reservation, so there is no
composition rethrow to omit. **The live mutant in those two modules is moving a stateful check in front of
the reservation** — which both compositions' own documentation invites, and which **silently converts a
replay into a re-decide.** That is precisely what these four tests cannot see, so pin against *that*
mutation, not against Training's.

**And a correction to how the earlier result should be read**, from the census itself: Training's helper
drives 14 tests and **does not discriminate on its own** — Training pinned the property once, separately.
*"Training fixed it"* must not be read as *"Training's fourteen now discriminate."*

**21 of the 36 do discriminate, and not by accident** — the Meals backstops pass their failure gate only to
the first call and build a plain host for the retry, so the refusal's precondition is repaired for free.
That is the same discriminator, obtained structurally rather than written. **Do not disturb them.**


### Flag F-COERCION-MAKES-A-ZERO — three formatters turn "we did not measure" into a measured zero
state: open
severity: warn
owner: @sven
clears_when: no render path coerces null or undefined to a number, and each of the three known coercions is pinned with null, undefined and empty-string asserted separately from a genuine zero
cleared_by: L-MRG-COVERAGE-UNKNOWN

**The estate's most-repeated defect has a single mechanical cause, and it is now named.**

Sven's standing ruling is **withhold rather than zero**: a number that cannot be established must say so.
Four lanes have now removed a violation of it — a delivery record flipped to *Delivered* regardless of push
outcome, an accounting export reporting a store count while no provider existed, and **two in one module in
one day**:

- `Number(null)` is **`0`** — an absent projection lag rendered as *"0 poster står igjen"*.
- `Intl.NumberFormat().format(null)` is the string **`"0"`** — a per-reason count the server **withheld**
  printed as a counted zero.

**Both were found by the lane's own test, not by review**, which is the part worth keeping: the coercion is
invisible at the call site and only appears when someone writes the absent case down.

**The distinction that closes it is `=== null`, not falsiness.** `!0` is `true`, so a truthiness guard
swallows the genuine zero — which is the case that must survive. A lane that fixes this by testing
truthiness has replaced one wrong answer with another.

**And the middle world is what proves it.** Three worlds are needed, not two: a value present, a value
**genuinely zero**, and the value absent. Without the middle one, a surface that always says *unknown*
passes — the relabelling that looks like a fix.

A third instance is already recorded and unfixed: `readWasteEntries` was verified, but the **backend half**
of that contract could not be checked from the frontend repo, so *"web and API deploy independently, the
absent-block window is permanent"* stands as an unverified claim rather than a confirmed one.


### Decision D-MEALS-FINALIZE-OWNER — which surface owns the irreversible statement freeze
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-MEALS-STATEMENT-SURFACE
options:
| close-owns-it — the month-close surface keeps the freeze and the statements page links to it ; pro: it is the only surface whose refusal names the exception blocking it, which needed a join of the queue against a count-only problem document ; con: the three-stage walk stays impossible from one page until a link is added, so the exit that asked for it cannot be met as written
| statements-owns-it — move the freeze to the statements page and strip it from the close ; pro: draft, finalize and export then live on one surface and the walk is one journey ; con: the naming join moves with it or is lost, and losing it returns the estate to a refusal that says a count and names nothing
| both-with-one-link — close keeps the freeze, statements gains a link from the close carrying the run id ; pro: the page already reads that query param, so this is one link and no second control ; con: two surfaces still show statement state, and the operator has to know which one freezes
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: operators are observed mis-locating the freeze in use, in which case consolidate onto the surface that can name what is blocking it
ruled: both-with-one-link 2026-08-05 by @sven

**Named by `L-MEALS-STATEMENT-SURFACE` when it returned `blocked` rather than dressing a partial as met,
and it is a decision the plan did not have.**

Two lanes were found binding the same irreversible freeze — recorded as `F-TWO-FINALIZE-CONTROLS`, caught
by a lane **watching the shared checkout go dirty under it**, not at a merge. Told to consume rather than
duplicate, it did: **it built no second finalize control and no second draft control.**

**The consequence is that its own exit became unreachable.** That exit names three stages walked in a
browser; a browser *control* walked one. Draft and finalize went through the API context, **labelled `API`
in their own step names inside the artifact** rather than presented as browser steps.

**The seam it took was one the sibling had drawn itself** — that lane's own client header records which
statement reads are *"deliberately still absent"*, and those are exactly the three this lane took. So the
family is now bound once per half, which is the outcome the flag wanted.

**What the walk did prove is not nothing**, and the structural fact under it is the reason this matters:
`MealsStatementLine` carries **no membership id and no user id at all** — there is nothing on the payload
to reconstruct the reference from, so printing it is a persistence claim rather than a rendering one. Two
browser mutants red it at the right steps, one proving the CSV assertion is not carried by the screen.

The lane's own recommendation is `both-with-one-link`, and it is the cheapest: **the page already reads
the query param.**



**Fable recommends `both-with-one-link`, and the surfaces already say so themselves.** The statements page
reads a run id from the query and auto-opens; its own header records **why the freeze must stay beside the
exception queue** — *"two controls for one irreversible act, on two screens, means an operator can find the
one that cannot tell them what is stopping it"* — and explicitly notes that whoever merges the two **owes that
one link.**

**The other surface is already composed into the candidate and carries no such link yet**, so this is
genuinely one link carrying the run id. Giving the freeze to the statements page alone would **detach an
irreversible act from the only surface that can name the row blocking it** — the named-refusal capability the
estate just built.

### Lane L-XZ-SIGNED-COUNT — a negative goods-group count stops being restated as a smaller one
state: verified
class: suite
pts: 1
exit: a goods-group row whose quantity is negative keeps its digits and its sign at the widths where the label must shorten, pinned by a world the existing sweep never sampled, recorded in lanes/L-XZ-SIGNED-COUNT/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-XZ-SIGNED-COUNT/mutation-log.md

**A Fable review reproduced this against the real builder rather than arguing it, and printed the output.**

The choke-point fit rule requires an **all-digit** trailing group. **`'-'` is not a digit**, so a goods-group
row whose net quantity is negative fails the test and **the whole label, count included, is shortened as
prose**:

```
GoodsGroup { Name = "Sesongens smaksmeny", Quantity = -12, Amount = -123400 }
prints:  Sesongens smaksmeny (… -1 234,00
```

At nearby widths it prints `(-12…` — **−123 restated as −12.** The wrong-and-plausible form again, and **on
a returns-dominated day, which is an ordinary day.**

**The goods-group net quantity is the one count on the document that can go negative** — every statutory
count accumulates `+= 1` and is safe. So the commit's claim that one change covers every count-bearing row
**is false in this regime**, and the sweep that proved the rest — counts of 1, 9, 12, 127, 1234 — **never
sampled a signed count.**

The reviewer named the change: allow one optional `'-'` immediately after the opening parenthesis before
requiring digits, keeping the at-least-one-digit rule, so a signed trailing count is excluded from
shortening exactly like an unsigned one. **Pin it with a world the sweep did not have**, asserting the count
reads its sign and carries no ellipsis after the last parenthesis.

**This is the third time this defect has been fixed at a scale that missed the next one.** The first shrank
a label against one world; the second protected unsigned counts at five widths. **Add the sign to the
sweep, not just to the rule.**

### Lane L-CENSUS-CORRECTIONS — the two censuses stop teaching rules their own evidence does not support
state: verified
class: analysis
pts: 1
exit: the six named corrections are applied to the two census documents, each citing what falsified it, and no immunity rule remains that a later needle or registration could inherit falsely, recorded in lanes/L-CENSUS-CORRECTIONS/evidence.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-CENSUS-CORRECTIONS/evidence.md

**A Fable review verified both censuses independently — re-running one extractor, writing its own exact
dynamic program and a two-million-sample Monte Carlo, and reading every cited site. Every load-bearing
finding held. Six statements did not, and each is the kind that outlives the document.**

**1. The aliasing census's immunity rule is mis-derived.** It enumerated randomness in the **test tree**
and concluded that any needle whose alphabet exceeds hex is safe. But **haystacks are produced by
production code invoked in-test**, and production mints randoms with wider alphabets — url-safe base64
preference tokens, a random-nonce encrypted address in standard base64, an invitation token, a decimal
confirmation code. **The census's own row 6 is the existence proof of that class.**

The reviewer then did the work the rule skipped: extracted all 14 short alphanumeric non-hex needles and
checked each against its actual haystack. **The class is clear at this tip** — nothing was missed. But
the rule as written would call a base64-bearing haystack *P = 0*, so **the next needle added under it
inherits a false clearance.**

**2. The DI census's summary table says a site is unguarded when it is not** — the guard exists in a
contract test that reds on a dropped registration line. **The prose hedged; the table did not.** And the
observation that matters beyond this fix: **the table is what dispatches lanes.** A hedge in the body does
not stop a row from becoming work.

**3. The arithmetic is right and one argument for it is backwards** — exactly what the review brief
suspected. `"250"` **cannot overlap itself**, so overlapping windows contribute about 0.2%; the real
correction is that **two of the twenty-two windows are impossible**, because the version nibble is pinned
and the variant nibble is constrained. And *"both figures were optimistic"* has the direction wrong: they
**overstate** the failure rate.

Also: two categorical immunity claims are false as universals — one assertion form does carry needles, and
**19 of 120 predicate-form assertions embed literal substring searches.** All are immune **by alphabet**,
not by the overload semantics the census gives as the reason. **A right verdict with a wrong reason is a
rule that fails the next time.**

**Nothing here invalidates a dispatched lane.** The corrections are to what the documents teach, not to
what they found.

### Flag F-LAND-OUTBOX-FLAKE-NOT-GUID — of the two rival fixes, one catches a leak the other misses
state: open
severity: warn
owner: @sven

### Flag F-TRANSLATIONS-ARE-A-CHOKE — three shared files nobody can safely commit
state: open
severity: warn
owner: @sven
clears_when: every lane's translation work is committable without sweeping a sibling's, and no lane reports finished work it could not commit
cleared_by: L-MRG-RECIPE-REVISE-UI

**`L-MRG-RECIPE-REVISE-UI` finished its work and could not commit it.** Verified: all three of
`translations/{no,en,de}.ts` are modified in the shared checkout by siblings, and **no pathspec commit is
safe without sweeping somebody else's edits.** So a lane's completed, mutation-proven work sits
uncommitted in a worktree.

**This is the estate's rules working correctly and producing a jam.** Commit by pathspec, never
`git add -A`, never clean what you did not dirty, never bulk-edit these three files — every one of those
is right, and together they mean the busiest shared files in the frontend have no safe write path once two
lanes want them in the same hour.

**The reason the no-bulk-edit rule exists is not negotiable**: a conflict resolved that way once shipped
the app with **no client bundle**. So the fix is not to relax it.

The consequence to hold on to: **uncommitted work is the most fragile state in this program.** A killed
session recovered ten lanes from committed branches today; the one thing that recovery could not have
saved is a worktree nobody had committed.

Options worth ruling: a per-lane translation fragment merged at land time; a lane-owned lock on the three
files; or an explicit convention that a lane commits its translation lines **and** the siblings' lines it
found, naming them — which is honest but makes every lane a partial merge of every other.


**A way through it was found on 2026-08-04, and it is recorded here because it departs from what this flag
told lanes to do.** `L-MRG-REVISE-LAND` was briefed to leave all translation work alone. Measured, that
made its exit unreachable: the 36KB test reads the translation tables directly at lines 824-835, so at the
translation-free commit `0c483de` the suite is **49/51 with exactly those two tests red**.

**So it landed the translations as a second, separate commit** — `c429d51`, sixteen lines per locale and
nothing else — and wrote down the undo: `git update-ref refs/heads/lane/mrg-recipe-revise-ui 0c483de`
restores the briefed boundary exactly.

**The rule was respected rather than relaxed, which is the part worth keeping.** The hunk was built against
`5ad0ca0`'s **committed** file through a temporary index — never the dirty working tree — and its extractor
refuses unless every hunk is a pure addition, hunk 1 holds exactly the fourteen `mrg_revise_*` keys the
lane's evidence claims, no `mlst_`, `mrgs_` or `nav_meals` key leaked in, and zero committed lines are
deleted. Sixty lines per locale belonging to other lanes were **left behind**, named, for their owners.

**What this suggests about the options above.** The jam is not the three files; it is *bulk* edits and
*sweeping a sibling*, and both can be avoided per-hunk against the committed blob. That is close to the
third option already listed — a lane committing its own lines — minus the part that made it unattractive,
because the extractor proves the boundary instead of asking a lane to be careful. Whether that becomes the
convention is still Sven's to rule; what is settled is that one lane did it, showed its work, and made it
reversible with a single command.

### Lane L-HOSTED-SERVICE-FLOOR — deleting a background registration stops being invisible
state: built-unverified
class: suite
pts: 2
exit: every production IHostedService not on a written exemption list has a registration the floor can see, and deleting any one reds, pinned outside the wire tier because that tier strips them, recorded in lanes/L-HOSTED-SERVICE-FLOOR/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-HOSTED-SERVICE-FLOOR/mutation-log.md

**Named by two lanes and left by both, with the constraint that makes it awkward measured rather than
guessed.**

`AddHostedService` deletion is **invisible today**: the containment guard counts **types**, not
registrations, so it stays green with every registration line deleted. And the reachability sweep's module
mapping is namespace-scoped, so **four of the ten — including both money loops,
`PaymentCaptureBackgroundService` and `DailyMaintenanceBackgroundService` — are unswept.**

**The constraint, from the lane that just built the sibling floor:**
`WireHost.RemoveApplicationHostedServices` **strips every application hosted service from the test host**,
so **the wire tier structurally cannot floor a hosted-service registration.** Read `Registrations`
**before** that removal, or work outside the tier entirely. A floor written inside it would be green in
every world.

**Two shapes already measured that your floor must avoid.**
- **A count floor is not a floor.** The telemetry sibling proved it: the framework registers ten
  initializers of its own, **not one of which redacts anything**, so a count fact **passes** under the very
  deletion it was meant to catch. **Name the types with `typeof`** so a rename or deletion breaks
  compilation rather than silently matching nothing.
- **A guard against a throwaway collection has the same hole as a source-text guard, one layer along** —
  it stays green the day somebody deletes the *call* to the helper it invokes. That sibling departed from
  its own brief for exactly this reason and recorded why; do the same if you find a better shape, and say
  so.

All ten registrations sit inside the composition helpers a reflection seam can invoke, so a
`ServiceCollection`-level assertion is buildable — a reviewer verified that independently.

**Non-vacuity:** delete **each** registration separately and show each reds. A floor that reds on "none at
all" but not on "this one missing" is a floor for the wrong failure. And the exemption list must be
**written**, not implied: an unlisted service that nobody registered should red, not pass quietly.


### Flag F-THE-FIX-REPRODUCED-THE-DEFECT — a lane's own count made the same mistake it was fixing
state: open
severity: info
owner: @sven
clears_when: no lane's success criterion aggregates over a set wider than the thing it claims succeeded
cleared_by: L-ACCOUNTING-EXPORT-SILENT

**The clearest instance this program has produced of a defect surviving its own fix, and the lane reported
it rather than quietly correcting it.**

The defect: an accounting export reported a store count taken from **a different query** than the one that
did the exporting, so **the books went unposted while the job said it ran.**

The lane's first cut asserted the result list had three entries — which held **only because its own POS
double returned nothing.** Worse, and this is the finding: its success criterion aggregated `Success`
**over a merged list**, which **would have counted a store as exported on the strength of its Z-report
vouchers while its daily books went unposted.**

**That is the original defect, rebuilt inside the test written to catch it** — a success computed over a
set wider than the thing being claimed. The shape is identical: a number that is not wrong about what it
measured, measuring the wrong thing.

It split the two result sets, required the daily half non-empty and all-successful separately, and made
the fixture post POS vouchers for **deliberately not the set the daily export serves** — so the two can
never be confused again.

**Two smaller notes worth keeping from the same day.** Its mutant initially escaped its own dedicated test
because the refusal already failed that store, so it extended **the assertion** — a registered provider
that simply does not serve that store, no wiring gap and no refusal. And a sibling on the day settlement
found the reverse discipline: its first mutant **reds on the first assertion and cannot reach the ones
behind it**, so it wrote two more mutants rather than let later assertions ride on one that never ran.


### Lane L-COERCION-WRITE-PATHS — a coerced zero on a write path is worse than on a render
state: verified
class: node
pts: 1
exit: every remaining numeric coercion in the margin read models is classified as render-side or write-side, and each write-side one distinguishes null from zero, recorded in lanes/L-COERCION-WRITE-PATHS/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-COERCION-WRITE-PATHS/mutation-log.md

**Carried forward by `L-MRG-COVERAGE-UNKNOWN` after it committed its own work: *"worth checking whether any
other `|| 0` feeds a write path rather than a render; the ones I removed were all read-side."***

**The distinction it drew is the point of the lane.** A coerced zero on a **render** tells the reader a
number nobody measured. A coerced zero on a **write** changes what is sent. A sibling found the sharper
form: on a field where `null` means *no trim loss* and the server **refuses** `0`, the coercion did not
misreport anything — **it made a legitimate no-op save impossible.**

So the classification is the deliverable: **render-side or write-side, per site.** A render-side
coercion is the family already recorded as `F-COERCION-MAKES-A-ZERO`; a write-side one is a different and
worse defect wearing the same three characters.

**The distinction that closes each is `=== null`, not falsiness** — `!0` is `true`, so a truthiness guard
swallows the genuine zero, which is the case that must survive. And **three worlds, not two**: present,
genuinely zero, absent. Without the middle one, a surface that always says *unknown* passes.

**Report sites you rule safe as well as sites you fix.** A census that does not distinguish
checked-and-safe from not-checked is indistinguishable from silence, which is a failure this program has
already removed from two other documents.

### Lane L-MRG-INGREDIENT-FACTOR-ZERO — a withheld conversion factor stops printing as zero
state: open
class: node
pts: 1
exit: the ingredient panel renders a withheld conversion factor as withheld rather than as 0 while a stated 0 still renders as 0, pinned by a test that reds when the guard is removed, recorded in lanes/L-MRG-INGREDIENT-FACTOR-ZERO/mutation-log.md
needs: F-MRG-INGREDIENT-FACTOR-ZERO

**Both the finding and its confirmation are already on the record**, so this lane starts from a measured
site rather than a search: `components/admin/margin/MarginIngredientPanel.vue:146`, unguarded
`number(conversion.factorToBase)`, `format(null)` rendering `"0"`.

**Three worlds, not two** — present, genuinely zero, withheld. The closing distinction is `=== null`, not
falsiness. Without the middle world a panel that always says *unknown* passes.

**One refinement from the sibling that found this, worth applying rather than rediscovering:** the
falsiness trap is a property of the value's **domain**, not of the idiom. `!0` is `true`, but `!'0'` is
`false` — so a guard over a string field enforces nothing, and a test written against one can never fail.
`factorToBase` arrives off the wire as a number or `null`, which is the domain where the rule bites.

`supersededConversions` reads `detail.conversions` straight off the wire with no read model. Decide
deliberately whether the distinction belongs in a read model or at the render, and say which and why.

**Drive the pin through the rendered panel, not through the formatter.** A formatter test would pass on
every one of the defects this lane exists to close — the shape has been found three times this session,
most recently as a page suite that pinned none of its four controls because it called the handlers
directly.


### Lane L-LANES-OUT-OF-THE-ASSEMBLY — a file parked under lanes/ stops compiling into the product
state: built-unverified
class: suite
pts: 1
exit: a .cs file placed under lanes/ is excluded from the WebApi assembly, shown by a build that succeeds with a deliberately broken lane file present and reds if the exclusion is removed, recorded in lanes/L-LANES-OUT-OF-THE-ASSEMBLY/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-LANES-OUT-OF-THE-ASSEMBLY/mutation-log.md

**An estate-level hazard, found by `L-HOSTED-SERVICE-FLOOR` while building something else and confirmed
loudly by its reviewer.** `WebApi.csproj:9-12` removes only `WebApi.Tests/**`. **Anything else parked under
`lanes/` compiles into the production assembly** — evidence drivers, scratch harnesses, a half-written
helper somebody left behind.

**Zero `.cs` files sit under `lanes/` today, which is exactly why this is worth doing now.** The hazard is
waiting for the first lane that forgets, and by then the failure arrives as a mysterious build error or, far
worse, as a type that quietly ships. The finding lane worked around it by keeping its drivers in Python —
a workaround that holds only while every future lane remembers the same thing.

The named change: add `<Compile Remove="lanes/**" />` at `WebApi.csproj:9`, with matching `Content`,
`EmbeddedResource` and `None` removes so no lane file reaches the assembly by another route.

**It is its own lane because it touches a production file** and the lane that found it deliberately touched
none. Keep it that small: this is a one-line exclusion plus the proof that it holds.

**Prove it by planting, not by reading.** Put a deliberately uncompilable `.cs` under `lanes/`, show the
build succeeds with the exclusion and reds without it, then remove the plant. A csproj assertion that only
greps the file would pass on a project where the glob does not match what anyone thinks it matches.



**Built at `2c1eebaf`, and the planting found a second route the brief never named — a worse one.**
`Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` globs `**/*.json` as `Content` with `CopyToOutputDirectory`, so a `.json` parked
under `lanes/` **reaches `bin/` and publish without ever compiling**. No red, no warning. The lane watched
a plant land at `bin/Debug/net8.0/lanes/.../plant-content.json` **on a green build**.

**That is the "quietly ships" failure this lane was written to prevent, and `Compile` alone would have left
it wide open.** The three non-`Compile` removes were asked for out of caution; they now have evidence
behind them. Item counts under `lanes/` moved `Compile 1→0, Content 1→0, None 23→0` — the twenty-three
being every tracked lane evidence file, already inside the project before this change.

**Two notes carried forward rather than acted on.**

*Recorded and reasoned, deliberately left open:* repo-root `lanes/` does **not** reach `WebApi.Tests.csproj`, whose globs are
rooted at `WebApi.Tests/` — plant-validated as a negative, since the same evaluation did detect a
test-local plant. But `WebApi.Tests/lanes/` **would** compile. The lane left it: no such directory exists,
it is not the convention, a test assembly never ships, and the failure there is loud and local. Cheap
symmetry if anyone wants it; widening would have exceeded the one-production-file scope.

*An instrument honesty note worth keeping:* the lane's final state initially returned in 1.07s as
up-to-date. Legitimate — the plant was already excluded a state earlier, so removing it changes no input —
but **indistinguishable from the stale-build trap this estate documents**, so it re-ran with
`--no-incremental` (18.8s, fresh assembly mtime) and recorded only that. A build that is right for the
wrong reason reads exactly like one that is wrong.

### Lane L-JOURNEY-PORT-HARDCODED — a journey spec stops being green only on the default port
state: verified
class: node
pts: 1
exit: meals-statement-month runs green on a non-default fixture port as four sibling specs already do, shown by a run on a non-default port recorded in lanes/L-JOURNEY-PORT-HARDCODED/evidence.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-JOURNEY-PORT-HARDCODED/evidence.md

**Found the only way it could be found — by running on a non-default port.** `L-JOURNEY-MEALS` did, and
`test/e2e/journeys/meals-statement-month.spec.js:72` **hard-codes 4010** and ignores `E2E_FIXTURE_PORT`.
**Four sibling specs read the variable correctly**, so this is one file out of step rather than a
convention nobody adopted.

**Why it is worth a lane rather than a note.** A spec that is green only on the default port is green only
when nothing else is running — and this program routinely walks several journeys at once, which is exactly
when a second fixture needs a second port. The failure it produces is not a clear refusal; the walk talks
to **somebody else's fixture** and reports on a world it did not build.

The finding lane hit precisely that: its non-default run reddened the spec and **displaced a sibling's
canonical artifact**. It kept the superseded copy and restored green on 3010/4010 rather than leaving the
damage, which is why this is a small lane and not a recovery.

**Prove it on a non-default port**, not by reading the diff. A test that reads `E2E_FIXTURE_PORT` and is
only ever run on 4010 is indistinguishable from one that ignores it.


**Built, and the red was proved at the wire rather than by running the broken walk.** The lane
**deliberately declined** to run the unfixed spec: its first use of that base is a mutating POST creating a
statement draft, followed by an **irreversible finalize**, and `127.0.0.1:4010` was held by a **live
fixture belonging to another lane**. Running it would have created and finalized a statement inside a
sibling's world.

Instead it asked both expressions who answers them, from a lane-local run on 4318: the old base got
**HTTP 200 from the foreign fixture, reporting `port: 4010`**, while the run's own fixture was 4318.
**That is the dangerous form of this failure — not a refusal, but a stranger's world answering
successfully**, which is why a spec pinned to a default port fails silently rather than loudly.

Green proved on **two** non-default port pairs (4318/3318 and 4319/3319), 12/12 each, `foreignSubjectServed:
0`, because one port would have been weak evidence of portability.

**A displacement that could not be avoided by choosing a port**, handled rather than ignored: the fixture
backend key is the constant `"fixture"` regardless of port, so **any** port writes the same canonical slot.
The lane backed up all four slots first, the store reported `supersedes: null`, and the displaced record
plus its three screenshots are preserved whole in the lane directory.

**A fragility this lane found and could not fix: the spec it repaired is untracked on this branch.** It
belongs to an unmerged sibling lane, so the fix rides in the working tree until that lane commits — and
**if that lane rewrites the file wholesale the fix disappears with no conflict to warn anyone.** That is
the same family as the dangling commits recorded under `F-COMMIT-TREE-LEAVES-NO-REF`: work that exists
without anything holding it.


### Lane L-OFFER-PARTIAL-SUBTOTAL — a subtotal stops presenting a partial sum as a whole one
state: verified
class: node
pts: 1
exit: an offer whose line has no stated fee renders a subtotal that says so rather than a smaller number, pinned over a stated fee, a genuine zero and an absent one, recorded in lanes/L-OFFER-PARTIAL-SUBTOTAL/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-OFFER-PARTIAL-SUBTOTAL/mutation-log.md

**Found by `L-PRICE-CLEANUP-TWO` outside its own scope, measured on a real mount rather than reasoned
about, and deliberately not improvised into that diff.**

`components/shared/OfferDocument.vue` totals its lines with `(item.monthlyFee * item.quantity || 0)`, so
**an unstated fee is summed as nothing.** The measured render: the lines read
`["kr 499,00", "—"]` while the subtotal beneath prints **`kr 499,00`**.

**That combination is the defect, and it is worse than either half alone.** The line is honest — it says it
does not know the fee. The total then quietly treats *unknown* as *zero* and presents a partial sum as a
whole one. A reader who trusts the line has every reason to trust the total, and the document gives them
no way to tell the two apart.

**It is user-visible**, unlike the two traps that lane was sent to remove: the offer document is reachable
at `/offer/:code` and `/admin/offers`, and an offer is a document somebody quotes a price from.

The right home is `statedSum` and `test/price-bypass-legacy.test.js`, which already own this family.

**Three worlds, not two** — a stated fee, a genuine zero, and an absent one. The middle case is the one a
truthiness guard eats, and `!0` is `true`, so `|| 0` cannot be replaced by another falsiness test.
**Decide deliberately what a partial subtotal should say** and record the reasoning: refusing to total at
all, totalling what is stated and marking it partial, and printing the absence mark are all defensible, and
they are not the same promise to a reader.

**Check the other totals in the same document before closing.** One line of this shape usually has
siblings, and a fix to the one that was found leaves a document that is right in the place somebody looked.

### Lane L-OFFERS-PAGE-HUNDREDFOLD — four offer helpers that are both unguarded and off by a hundred

naming what actually resolves, precisely so the next reader would not re-derive the same wrong conclusion.

**If you keep them, prove the magnitude with a real figure**, not by reading: a helper that divides by 100
before a formatter expecting minor units renders `kr 4,99` where `kr 499,00` was meant, and that is the kind
of error a test written from the same misunderstanding will happily confirm.

**Three worlds, not two** — a stated amount, a genuine zero and an absent one — and the closing distinction
is `=== null`, not falsiness.


**All four deleted, and the reason is the interesting part.** Repairing them would have created **a second
answer to "what does this offer total"** — and `OfferDocument`, rendered on this very page, is already the
correct one and now totals absence-honestly. Two helpers answering one question is how the next defect
gets written.

**The premise was re-proven rather than inherited.** It was told the four had zero call sites by a lane
working on a neighbouring file. It checked the template, computed properties, `this[...]`, `$options.methods`,
importers and `git -S` across **every ref** — every hit is a definition line, dead since the initial commit.
That is the check that made deletion defensible rather than merely tidy.

**The magnitude was executed, not read.** The helper rendered **`kr 4,99`** where the document renders
**`kr 499,00`** for the same 49900 øre — the hundredfold confirmed by running it, which matters because a
test written from the same misunderstanding would have confirmed the wrong figure just as happily. Absence
printed `kr 0,00`, and a stated zero was indistinguishable from an absent one.

**Two limits it stated rather than hid**, both correct to report: the suite was **skipped** because the host
stood at load 59.8, and its worktree lacks `35e5cdd`, so the `OfferDocument` beside it is the pre-fix copy —
left as found rather than quietly updated.


### Lane L-XZ-NEGATED-ABSENCE — six fiscal rows print a minus sign attached to the unknown mark
state: verified
class: node
pts: 1
exit: no report row renders a negated absent amount as a sign attached to the unknown mark, and a stated negative still renders, pinned over a stated amount, a genuine zero and an absent one, recorded in lanes/L-XZ-NEGATED-ABSENCE/mutation-log.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-XZ-NEGATED-ABSENCE/mutation-log.md

**Found by `L-PRICE-BYPASS-FIVE` and confirmed by mounting rather than reading** — which is why the count
is right. It was first reported as two rows; measured, it is **six**: `XReportView.vue:51`, `:54`, `:88`,
`:94`, `:97` and a per-operator row at `:178`. The rendered output was captured verbatim, e.g.
`"pos_report_negative_sales (2)−—"`.

**No gate can reach it, and that is the whole difficulty.** The minus is a **template literal outside the
interpolation** — `−{{ priceLabel(…) }}` — so the formatter never sees it. Every absence gate in the estate
runs inside the interpolation and is powerless here. The fix wants a `negatedAmountLabel` that owns the
sign, rather than another guard.

**Why this earns its own lane rather than riding a sibling's diff.** It changes **five shipped rows on a
fiscal document**, which is a kassasystemforskrifta artifact an inspector reads. A sign is not decoration
there: `−—` reads as a negative of an unknown, and a reader cannot tell it from a formatting slip.

**Three worlds, not two, and a fourth here**: a stated positive, a stated negative, a genuine zero, and an
absent amount. **A stated negative must still render its sign** — a fix that drops the minus to avoid `−—`
trades a confusing row for a wrong one.

**C6 governs**: do not widen statutory naming and do not add a § reference. Prove it by mounting, as the
finding lane did — a source-level assertion cannot see a literal sitting outside an interpolation.


### Lane L-GR-EXIT-WIRE-THE-MAIL — the working exit gets linked from the mail that carries it
state: verified
class: node
pts: 2
exit: a dispatched message's footer carries a link to the session-free unsubscribe page and a browser opening it completes a withdrawal, shown by the J-EXIT-UNSUB journey capture recorded in lanes/L-GR-EXIT-WIRE-THE-MAIL/evidence.md
agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-GR-EXIT-WIRE-THE-MAIL/evidence.md

**Ruled remedy for `F-GR-NO-EXIT-FROM-A-LIST`, and the assessment overturned the defect's own framing.**
Sven's instruction was to review and go with the recommendation; this is phase 1 of it, and it **needs no
deployment change**.

**The session-free exit already exists and is already correct.** `POST /v1/growth/unsubscribe`
(`Controllers/GrowthPreferenceController.cs:143`) is token-only and RFC 8058-shaped, needing no cookie; and
`pages/preferences/unsubscribe.vue` is fully built to spend it — it reads `#token=`/`?token=`, strips it
from the address bar at `:160-167`, and posts through a client that sends **no** `credentials:'include'`, so
it works under today's non-credentialed CORS.

**The whole defect is one missing join.** `GrowthMarketingFooter.cs` links **only** the session-based
preference centre — whose session is unopenable cross-site — and **nothing anywhere emits a link to the
page that works.**

**The five named changes**, all backend, all on the integration branch:
`GrowthSettings.cs` gains `UnsubscribePageBaseUrl` with the same fail-closed posture as
`PreferenceCentreBaseUrl:53`; a new `GrowthUnsubscribePageLink.cs` mirrors `GrowthPreferenceCentreLink:38-66`
and returns `{base}#token=<unsubscribe token>` — **fragment, never query, because C7 means the browser must
never transmit it**; `GrowthMarketingFooter.cs:45` and `:58` take the page URI and render a second, plain
"meld deg av" link beside the existing one; `GrowthDispatchService.cs:499-500` builds it from the token
already minted at `:465`; and a `[HttpGet("unsubscribe")]` beside the POST at `:143` **302s** to the page.

**That GET closes a hole nobody had listed**: a human who long-presses the List-Unsubscribe URI today gets
a **405**. A redirect is RFC-legal — only redirecting the POST is forbidden — and scanner-safe, because the
GET changes nothing.

**For a guest surface, the mail is the navigation entry**, which is how C3 is satisfied here. And
`unsubscribe.vue:102-108` currently says *nothing links here yet*; that sentence becomes false the moment
this lands and must go in the same change — C6 discipline in reverse.

**Accepted residual, stated rather than hidden:** the footer link lands on a page that unsubscribes on
arrival, so a scanner executing JavaScript could trigger it. The page has already ruled that one-click
means one-click; the machine path stays the header POST.

**Prove it by walking it**, not by suite: dispatch to a consented test contact, **copy the link out of the
captured message body rather than constructing it**, open it in a real browser, watch the done card, then
dispatch again and confirm the delivery goes `Suppressed` — withdrawal effective, not merely acknowledged.
Walk the long-press leg too.



**Built. The art. 7(3) obligation is satisfiable from this commit** — a dispatched footer now carries the
session-free exit, and a browser opening the **captured** link completes a withdrawal that **suppresses the
next campaign**. The long-press leg went from `405` to a `302` that changes nothing.

**The lane introduced a C7 violation and its own test caught it.** MVC's `Redirect()` makes
`RedirectResultExecutor` log the target — **fragment and token** — at Information, into a sink App Insights
retains. **The fragment was chosen precisely because it never reaches a server**, so that single log line
defeated the entire mechanism. Fixed by setting `Location` directly, mutation-checked both ways.

**It also found its own first green run partly vacuous.** The page strips its token on mount, so a later
`goto` differing only in the fragment is a same-document navigation and never remounts — the replay and
refusal legs were asserting against the previous arrival's card. **The token-dead leg then failed honestly
before it passed for real**, which is the only reason the green is worth anything.

**A ruling recorded so a future secret-scanner hit has an answer waiting.** The committed
`capture/captured-exit-link.txt` holds a real-*format* unsubscribe token and stays. The journey must open
the link **the dispatcher composed** — that composition is the property under test — and regenerating would
prove a constructed link instead. The token is dead by construction: minted into an in-memory database
destroyed at test exit, naming the fictional host `web.growth.test`.

**The lane refused the comfortable half of that ruling, and was right to.** Asked whether its
`@fixture`/`grepInvert` arrangement structurally prevented regeneration against a real backend, it answered
**no** — that arrangement forbids *spending*, not regenerating, and regeneration happens in a backend xUnit
test Playwright's config has no reach over. **Everything that made the token inert was how that test
happened to be written, and none of it was enforced.** So `WriteEvidence` now refuses to write unless the
captured link names the fictional host, **with the host literal duplicated inside the guard rather than read
from the harness constant — a guard expressed in terms of the thing it guards cannot fail.** Mutation-checked:
repointed at a real host the test reds **and the evidence directory is never created**.

**Go-live still needs `Growth:UnsubscribePageBaseUrl` pointed at the real consumer-web origin**, which is
owner-applied and comes after the deployment steps already ordered under `F-PROD-CORS-WILDCARD`.

### Lane L-CORS-LAND-FOLLOWUPS — the named credentialed policy that already exists gets landed safely
state: verified
class: suite

agent: opus
evidence: lanes/L-CORS-LAND-FOLLOWUPS/evidence.md

**Ruled remedy for `F-PROD-CORS-WILDCARD`, and the assessment's headline was that most of it already
exists.** `lane/cors-followups` (tip `524289b9`, forked at `35696d6b`, **not** on the integration tip
`8e2b57de`) already implements a named, credentialed, derived-allowlist policy — the exact thing two
frontend comments describe and the integration tip does not have.

**The merge hazard is the reason this is a lane rather than a merge.** The lane **forked before
`BrowserReadableHeaders` existed**, so its extracted helper hardcodes `WithExposedHeaders("ETag")` while the
tip exposes `BrowserReadableHeaders.All` — ETag, **Content-Disposition** and **X-Meals-Content-Hash**.
Resolving the inevitable `Program.cs` conflict by taking the lane's extraction as-is **silently re-breaks
every download filename and the Meals content hash.** Port `BrowserReadableHeaders.All` into `AddOkamCors`
and prove a download still arrives named.

**Landing it breaks nobody**, which is what makes it safe now: it is additive, and the endpoints it governs
have **zero working callers today** — they die at preflight or 401.

**Do not retire the wildcard default in this lane.** That is a separate, later, observation-first change,
and coupling it here is the mistake the assessment names explicitly. The wildcard stays, without
credentials, on the reasoning the lane's own doc comment records: a bearer-token API where nothing rides on
ambient credentials.

**One caller nobody had listed, worth carrying into any later tightening:** `okam-swiss.ch` is built from
**this same repository** as a CH edition, and `nuxt.config.js:45` points **both** editions at the same API
unless `API_BASE_URL` is overridden at build time. It is the easiest browser caller to forget, and it would
be the first casualty of a tightened default.

**Distinguish browser callers from server-to-server ones.** Wolt, Vipps, Dintero, Stripe, Surfboard and
Postmark webhooks send no `Origin` and are not CORS-bound; the native consumer app uses native HTTP. **None
of them justifies a wildcard**, and exactly one credentialed browser family exists in the whole estate.

**Per the review protocol this lane gets its own dedicated reviewer**, and the `BrowserReadableHeaders.All`
port is the specific thing that reviewer must check.
