**Recommended:** compose-and-refuse — it is everything this machine can honestly show, and the refusal is
worth more than the assertion: today a missing origin produces a guest with no way back, silently.

"a live test-MSN initiate for a deposit returns a redirect and, after approval in Vipps, the guest lands back on the deposit page reading paid" — contradicted twice over. (1) No test MSN exists anywhere in the tree: VippsSettings ClientId/ClientSecret/OcpApimSubscriptionKey are the literal "Set in Azure. For development, set in User Secrets" placeholders, BaseUrl is the LIVE https://api.vipps.no, and OkamMsn 560743 is a production MSN. (2) Events:PublicBaseUrl — the guest web app origin that serves the deposit page — is unset in EVERY committed configuration (appsettings.json's Events section holds only DispatchEnabled:false; appsettings.Development.json has no Events section at all), and its own doc comment records that which origin serves those pages "remains Sven's decision". So there is neither a credential to initiate with nor an address to return the guest to, and the guest could not have been mailed the link in the first place. Corrected exit: "a deposit initiate composes merchantInfo.fallBack as {Events:PublicBaseUrl}/events/deposit/{token}, asserted on the JSON body the real VippsService posts, and refuses to create the Vipps order at all when no such origin is configured; the approve-and-return leg is deferred to the first test-MSN harness after Sven sets Events:PublicBaseUrl."
### Decision D-SPEC-L-GR-WITHDRAW-ORIGIN — which origin serves the guest surfaces
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-GR-WITHDRAW-ORIGIN
options:
| api-subdomain — point the API base at the existing `api.okam.no` and name the origins in CORS ; pro: **it is already live infrastructure** — the same App Service, same address, valid certificate, health answering — and it shares the registrable domain with the web app, so the two are the **same site** and the Strict cookie is attached with **no change to the cookie at all**; the hardening survives ; con: it binds the Events guest origin too, which must then also sit under that domain or the same problem reopens there later
| samesite-none — keep the current hosts and relax the cookie to none-with-secure ; pro: works, and changes no DNS ; con: **it gives up the browser's own cross-site protection**, leaving only the double-submit token — a real reduction traded for nothing the first option does not already provide
| reverse-proxy — serve the API same-site under the web origin ; pro: the shape the review originally proposed ; con: **unavailable — the web app is a static export on Pages and cannot proxy.** Recorded so it is not proposed again
default_if_unruled: none
ruled: api-subdomain 2026-08-03 by @sven
reopen_when: the Events guest origin cannot sit under the same registrable domain, so the same-site property is lost anyway

**Recommended:** api-subdomain — it is the only option where **nothing is given up**, and the infrastructure
it needs already exists and answers.

**Two things a same-origin test could never have produced, and the lane built a harness that could.** The
CORS fix is **unconditional** — the wildcard blocks a credentialed preflight *even same-site*, because the
call is still cross-**origin**. And *move the cookie off Strict*, implemented as **Lax** — the obvious
reading of that phrase, and the one my brief invited — **is still broken**: Lax rides top-level navigations,
never a fetch. **Anyone choosing Lax ships a fix that presents as a mystery 401.**

**The exit could not be met for a reason neither option addresses:** the deployed preference centre answers
404. **The Growth guest surface is unshipped** — it exists only on this branch, and the workflow deploys a
different one. No change in that lane could put a browser in front of a working deployed page.

"a browser at the deployed preference-centre URL shows the session cookie attached on the preferences read, answering 200" — https://okam.no/preferences/communications answers 404. The Growth guest surface is unshipped: it exists only on feature/restaurant-modules and .github/workflows/nuxtjs.yml deploys main only. Closing it also needs a redeploy of the API's CORS policy, which is the reserved topology decision.
### Decision D-SPEC-L-UTLKVIT-REPRINT-KIND — the plan contradicts what L-UTLKVIT-REPRINT-KIND observed
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-UTLKVIT-REPRINT-KIND
options:
| take-the-corrected-exit — keep JournalEntryId pointing at the sale, and pin the ROUND TRIP on the id the register actually hands a client ; pro: it is built, and its four pins address the expressions a client evaluates rather than an id SELECTed back out of the journal, which is what every prior pin did — deleting the forward resolution reds all eight ; con: the flag's original wording, "the model addresses it in the field a client actually reads", stays unsatisfied on paper and has to be rewritten
| move-the-field-as-briefed — put the delivery document's id in JournalEntryId ; pro: the model then addresses the handover document directly, which is what the flag asked for ; con: it makes a credit sale NON-REFUNDABLE AT THE TILL — the return path refuses any original whose receipt type is not Sale, and the refund modal calls straight through that field
| move-the-field-and-widen-the-return — do the above and teach the return path to accept a delivery original ; pro: both halves, no lost capability ; con: it widens what the refund path accepts inside kassasystemforskrifta territory, which is a much larger change than the defect justifies, and it removes a refusal that is currently load-bearing
default_if_unruled: none
ruled: take-the-corrected-exit 2026-08-03 by @sven
reopen_when: the return path is widened to accept a delivery original, at which point moving the field stops costing till refunds

Both halves are already closed at the base the brief itself sends me to, and the second half's prescribed remedy is harmful. Half 1 ("BuildReceiptAsync derives the kind from entry.ReceiptType ALONE") was true at lane/utlkvit-replay-source 3a509b68, where the brief was filed; L-UTLKVIT-SALE-ROW then added the third forward resolution in BuildDocumentForAsync, so at any base carrying BOTH lanes the SALREC of a credit sale already reprints as the utleveringskvittering through GET /pos/receipt/{id}, the print endpoint and the public page. Half 2's stated consequence ("a client reprinting from the natural field gets the wrong paper") is therefore false for the same reason: model.JournalEntryId is the sale's id, and the sale's id now resolves forward. Half 2's remedy - move JournalEntryId onto the delivery entry so the model "addresses it in the field a client actually reads" - would BREAK the register: FinalizeService.FinalizeReturnAsync refuses any original whose ReceiptType is not Sale, and RefundModal.vue calls RefundCash(receipt.journalEntryId), so a credit sale would become non-refundable at the till. Sale-row's choice (JournalEntryId stays the sale's; the sale resolves forward on read) is the correct one and must not be undone. Corrected exit, which I built: keep the field pointing at the sale and pin the ROUND TRIP on the id the register actually hands the client, since every pre-existing pin addresses an id read back out of the journal instead.

### Decision D-SPEC-L-MEALS-LEVER-WITHHOLD — the plan contradicts what L-MEALS-LEVER-WITHHOLD observed
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-MEALS-LEVER-WITHHOLD
options:
| retitle-and-pin — the lane's own recommendation: rename the descriptor to what it controls and pin the title against the measured reach ; pro: a one-line production change, no guard weakened, and it keeps the per-venue darkening that withholding would destroy ; con: the catalog keeps an entry of small operator value, so the confusion is reduced rather than removed
| withhold-anyway — apply the ruled withholding as briefed ; pro: consistent with the standing withhold-with-a-reason ruling already applied to Training and Workforce ; con: measured, it reds 8 of 28, and the blocker is a guard that has already ruled this question — a per-store-seam gate has no withholding escape hatch because the row it reads is writable only through the catalog-validated toggle API, so landing it means weakening that guard by hand and re-creating the Events.Settlement shape
| leave-as-is — neither retitle nor withhold ; pro: nothing changes and no guard is touched ; con: the title keeps reading as "Meals is on for this venue" while controlling four routes of thirty, which is the thing the lane was sent to remove
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: the per-store-seam guard is itself redesigned — nothing on the board proposes that today
ruled: retitle-and-pin 2026-08-05 by @sven

**The lane did not stop at reading, which is why these are worth ruling rather than re-deriving.** It
applied the withholding as a real candidate in the shape Training and Workforce already use, and
measured the same tree it mutated: **baseline 28/28 green, withholding applied 8 red / 20 pass, restored
28/28 green.**

**The brief's premise was false and it said so precisely.** *"A Meals switch that reaches nobody"* — off
the production assembly, `meals.module` gates **four store-addressed admin routes across three
services**. "None on the consumer path" is true; "reaches nobody" is not, and the standing ruling's
predicate is **advertised but does not gate**.

**The blocking guard's own failure text is the argument:** *"the row this gate reads can never be
written."* A gate resolved through the **per-store seam** must have its flag in the catalog and has no
withholding escape hatch; a gate resolved through **host config** may be withheld with a reason — which
is exactly why Meals' three existing withholdings are legal.

**And it named the real defect the brief was circling: the lie is in the title, not the advertisement.**
Flipping `meals.module` on delivers nothing usable — it lights a company directory you cannot create a
company in — while the title *"Module (store surfaces)"* reads as *"Meals is on for this venue"*.

Nothing in production changed: the flags file was mutated and restored byte-identical.

The brief rules withhold-with-a-reason on the premise of "a Meals switch that reaches nobody", but meals.module gates four store-addressed admin routes across three services -- measured off the production assembly -- so the standing ruling's predicate ("advertised but does not gate") does not hold for it. Contradicted by: applying the ruled withholding reds the landed guard MealsRouteGateReachabilityTests .Every_gate_a_meals_route_depends_on_is_settable_end_to_end, whose per-store-seam branch has no withholding escape hatch by design -- "the row this gate reads can never be written". Withholding this flag creates the Events.Settlement defect shape (enforced at four routes, no lever anywhere) rather than removing a lever that lies.

### Decision D-WOLT-HOSTED-EXEMPTION — whether the Wolt menu sync stays exempt from the hosted-service floor
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-HOSTED-SERVICE-FLOOR
options:
| keep-exempt — leave WoltMenuSyncBackgroundService on the written exemption list — pro: registering it starts live 8-minutely menu pushes to a third party, which is a commercial act and not an engineering one; the floor already reds both if somebody wires it and if the exemption goes stale, so it is dormant and guarded rather than dormant and forgotten ; con: the one background loop touching an external partner is the one loop with no positive floor, so nobody is told the day it should have been running
| register-and-gate — register it, with the outbound push held behind a lever the test host keeps down — pro: the exemption list empties and all ten loops carry the same floor ; con: it adds a production gate whose only consumer is a test, which is the shape C3 warns against, and a gate that fails open sends live pushes to a partner
| retire-it — delete the service if the Wolt menu sync is not a capability this product still intends — pro: an unregistered service that has never run on any branch is dead weight, and deleting it removes both the exemption and the question ; con: irreversible without the Wolt owner, and the dormancy may be deliberate rather than abandoned
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: the Wolt owner declares menu sync a wanted capability, at which point register-and-gate with a positive floor on the lever
ruled: keep-exempt 2026-08-05 by @sven

**The engineering half is already ruled and needs no further work.** An independent Fable review agreed the
exemption is correct as an engineering matter, having verified across **all branches** that no commit has
ever registered `WoltMenuSyncBackgroundService` in either fully-qualified or short form — the only similar
hits are an unrelated `AddScoped` sync service, comments, and the lane's own driver.

**What makes this yours is the consequence, not the code.** `Services/WoltMenuSyncBackgroundService.cs:21`
runs on `TimeSpan.FromMinutes(8)`, so registering it begins live third-party menu pushes. That is a
decision about a partner relationship.

**Nothing is exposed while this waits.** The service cannot run, because it is registered nowhere; wiring
it without a ruling reds the floor's exemption fact; and a new unlisted loop reds the completeness fact.
Both directions were proven by mutation, not asserted.



**Fable recommends `keep-exempt`, and in doing so corrects a claim this plan has been carrying.** The
containment floor was recorded here as counting **types rather than registrations**, so that it would stay
green with every registration line deleted. **At the tip it reads `graph.Registrations` filtered on
`AddHostedService`** — the clerk verified the source directly — and a companion assertion re-derives every
parked exemption and fails one that becomes reachable.

**So this service is dormant *and guarded*, not dormant and forgotten**, and the control names its invoker.
That makes it one of the estate's two exceptions to its own disease rather than another instance of it.
**Registering it instead would add a production lever whose only consumer is a test, and whose fail-open is a
live eight-minutely push to a partner.**

### Decision D-CREDITNOTE-SECOND-ISSUE — whether a second credit note against one invoice should be refusable
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-PDF-CREDITNOTE-NAME
options:
| allow-and-number — keep issuing, each under its own number, which is what now ships — pro: already built and pinned at the wire tier, partial credits keep working, and the two documents are distinguishable to a reader and to a filesystem ; con: a double click still issues a real second statutory document that somebody must then void, and nothing warns the operator it happened
| refuse-second — reject a credit note against an invoice that already has one — pro: one invoice, one credit note is what an accountant expects, and an accidental double click cannot silently produce a second bokføring document ; con: crediting two lines of one invoice separately is legitimate practice, so a blanket refusal breaks a real workflow to prevent a mis-click
| allow-with-confirmation — issue, but require an explicit confirmation when the invoice already carries a credit note — pro: keeps partial credits legal while making the second one deliberate rather than accidental ; con: it is a UI change on a path that has none today, and a confirmation on a routine action is the kind people learn to click through
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: a real line-subset credit-note capability lands, at which point allow-with-confirmation is the right shape and never allow-and-number
ruled: refuse-second 2026-08-05 by @sven

**Measured, not supposed.** `CreateCreditNote` **inserts unconditionally** — `L-PDF-CREDITNOTE-NAME` looked
for an already-credited check anywhere on the path and found none. So a double click issues a second
document, and until that lane landed, both arrived under **the same filename**, which is how the second one
could go unnoticed.

**The filename half is fixed and is not what this decision is about.** Two credit notes against invoice
990601 now serve as `KREDITNOTA-990602` and `KREDITNOTA-990603`, proven from the host's own log rather than
from a test assertion. What remains is the product question the lane deliberately did not answer: whether
the second document should exist at all.

**Why it is yours.** Refusing it is a change to what the product will let a bookkeeper do, and partial
credits are a real workflow — this is not a defect with an obviously correct fix.

**Fable recommends `refuse-second`, and the con shielding the other option describes a workflow this product
cannot perform.** The clerk verified it directly: the creation method takes **only an invoice id**, copies
**every line**, and `IsCreditNote = true` appears in **exactly one file, once**. **There is no partial-credit
capability**, so "crediting two lines separately is legitimate practice" is not a description of this system.

**Every second credit note is therefore a full double credit of the whole invoice**, minted by one
double-click on a live production endpoint — and under C1 it exists forever with nothing warning anyone. **A
one-per-invoice check breaks nothing that exists.**

**This is the only live production surface in its whole set.**

reopen_when: a ruling declares a ConsumerWeb branch for this program, which would make dropping and restoring dearer than waiting
ruled: clerk-does-it-both-probes 2026-08-05 by @sven

Removing a probe line and its fact span is a hand-edit of plan.md structure that no `plan` verb performs and that law L7 forbids a lane from making, contradicted by the CLI carrying no probe-mutation verb and by SPEC 1.2 assigning plan.md structure to humans.

**The lane was right to refuse, and it did the work anyway.** It extracted the verb set from the binary
rather than trusting `--help` — `init sign-off check refresh tick render serve headline start built verify
unverify accept retract decide flag note return log compact` — and **nothing mutates the probes fence.**
Every probe string in the tool is parse or validation. SPEC §1.2 assigns `plan.md` structure to humans;
§8 names the probes table as a hand-edited surface by design; L7's only exception is **additive**.

**A scope correction that changes the answer: two probes read that root, not one.**
`meals.token.client` (wire) and `cw.world` (meta). The ruling named the first. **Dropping only it leaves the
exit's second half false**, because `doctor` derives roots by grepping the whole fence and reads
`WORLD.json` from disk regardless.

**The order matters and was read off the tool, not guessed.** Span out first, line second, authored
references in the same edit: line-first raises `E-FACT-NO-PROBE`, a hard **error**; span-first degrades to
`W-PROBE-UNUSED`, a warning this plan already carries elsewhere.

**The item that makes this genuinely yours rather than clerical.** Dropping `meals.token.client` touches
five places — the probe line, the span, a `clears_when:`, a prose reference, and **the `exit:` of
`L-MEALS-FUNDED`, whose state is `verified`.** Rewriting a verified lane's exit changes what "verified"
meant for it. That is a judgement about evidence, not a deletion. Its other evidence half is a journey
artifact, so the real question is **whether that journey alone still carries the exit.**

**Census delivered regardless of the ruling — 33 probes over 3 roots**, and it separates checked-and-safe
from never-checked rather than reporting a single number: `.` — 8 probes, declared and conforming;
`../OkamAPI-modules` — 23 probes, declared but **MISMATCH**, which is the guard working and is already
ruled `already-guarded`; `../ConsumerWeb` — 2 probes, **UNDECLARED**, the only root that has never been
checked at all. **31 of 33 probes read a checked root**, and `MISMATCH` is not `UNDECLARED`.

**Fable recommends `clerk-does-it-both-probes`, and found the defect live on the board today.**
`fact:meals.token.client` is stamped **green as of 2026-08-04** on a root whose world **nobody declared** —
the clerk confirmed `on_expected` reads `unknown` on disk, and the doctor tags exactly that as undeclared. **A
green fact standing on unverified ground is this set's disease in its most direct form**, and
leave-both-and-restate would convert it into documentation.

**The cart-probe-only option measurably cannot meet the exit.** The genuinely owner-level part is that the
edit rewrites the exit of a lane already `verified` — that should be ruled explicitly as an evidence re-word,
in the measured order.


**Executed 2026-08-05 by the clerk, in the order the ruling specified.** Both fact spans removed first, both
probe lines second, and the two references rewritten in the same edit — the exit of the `verified` lane that
named the dropped fact, and a flag's clearing condition that read the same fact.

**The exit is met and was checked rather than assumed:** the doctor now lists two worlds and **no undeclared
root**. Before the edit, a fact was stamped green on a root whose world read `unknown`.

**The lane is retracted rather than dispatched**, because the ruling gave the work to the clerk and a session
spent re-deriving it would have produced the same three edits.

**One thing the same run surfaced and nothing had recorded:** the doctor reports the backend world as a
**MISMATCH** — the checkout sits on a lane branch, **missing four landed commits and carrying one unlanded**.
Every lane in this program has been told to read that repository with `git show <ref>:<path>` for exactly this
reason; **the mismatch is now visible in the instrument rather than only in the briefs.**

### Decision D-SPEC-L-TIER-ARTIFACTS — the plan contradicts what L-TIER-ARTIFACTS observed
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-TIER-ARTIFACTS
options:
| forward-only-plus-C8 — accept the convention and tooling as shipped, apply it to every lane from here, and add the proposed constraint so it reaches lane authors — pro: it is the only version of this that is honest, the tooling already works, and the constraint text reaches every author because intent constraints are copied verbatim into every generated brief ; con: it needs an intent amendment, which is yours alone, and it leaves ~361 existing branches with claims nobody can check
| forward-only-no-C8 — take the convention and tooling, put the rule in a document, and amend nothing — pro: no intent change and the tooling still works ; con: **measured, the rule already existed and was already unfollowable** — a well-written convention sat unread at `artifacts/tests/README.md` since 2026-07-31 while seven incompatible variants were in use, so filing it again is the option that has already been tried
| retrofit-anyway — attach a receipt to each existing branch now — pro: the count of unbacked claims goes to zero ; con: **it is the fabrication this lane exists to prevent** — a run executed today attached to an hours-old commit, and this lane's own two receipts differ by **36 tests at identical source** purely from harness state, so a fresh run demonstrably cannot stand in for the original
| declare-the-backlog — keep the forward rule and write the ~361 unbacked claims down as a known, dated gap — pro: honest and cheap, and it lets a reader tell which claims are checkable from which are not ; con: a number that large in a document tends to be read once and never acted on
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: the brief generator stops copying intent constraints verbatim, which is the mechanism that makes this rule reach lane authors at all
ruled: forward-only-plus-C8 2026-08-06 by @sven

Clause 1 is unsatisfiable honestly - ~361 lane branches carry tier claims against 8 receipts estate-wide, and any receipt added to them now would be a run executed today attached to an hours-old commit, contradicted by this lane's own two receipts which differ by 36 tests at identical source purely from harness state, proving a fresh run cannot stand in for the run a branch originally claimed.

**The second clause was delivered, so this ruling is about the backlog and the constraint, not about whether the work exists.** The convention and tooling ship on `lane/tier-artifacts` (`e34977ac..2a7bf12`, unpushed): the gitignore fixed so receipts can land in the clone at all, `record.sh` / `verify.js` / `to-junit.js` added, and two real receipts committed.

**Why it was unfollowable, measured rather than guessed — three independent causes, each now fixed:**
`artifacts/` was ignored as a **directory**, so git never descends and **no negation pattern could ever re-include it**; **nothing in either repository emits a trx or junit** (every `--logger trx` in the estate is prose *inside* a receipt, not a command anyone runs); and `jest-junit` is not installed. Nineteen uncommitted `.trx` files sit under `lanes/`, which is **not** gitignored. **The barrier was never technical — there was no rule saying which file, at which commit, is the record.**

**The C8 text is staged, not applied**, at `lanes/L-TIER-ARTIFACTS/proposed-C8.md`. The lane found that `plan`'s brief generator copies `intent.md` constraints **verbatim into every brief**, which makes that file the only text guaranteed to reach a lane author — and it is outside both its boundary and mine. **Amending intent is yours.**

**Fable recommends an option this block does not carry, and it should be written in before any ruling:
`forward-only-plus-C8`.** Neither existing option is what it would choose. **Retrofit is refuted by the lane's
own evidence** — two committed receipts from identical source differ by 36 tests, which is fabrication, not
recovery. And forward-only *without* the constraint is **literally the experiment that already failed on
2026-07-31.**

**What makes the third option different is that it names an invoker.** The brief generator copies intent
constraints verbatim into every brief, so a constraint reaches every future lane author by mechanism rather
than by their reading a README. **The roughly 361-branch backlog belongs as a dated note, not as fresh
receipts.**

### Decision D-SPEC-L-WF-INVITE-SURFACE — the plan contradicts what L-WF-INVITE-SURFACE observed
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-WF-INVITE-SURFACE
options:
| close-it-built — mark the lane satisfied by the work already at baseline, and open the backend gap as its own lane — pro: the surface, its routes, its nav entries and a green browser walk all exist and were re-verified by an independent 16/16 walk, so the lane's objective is met and only its author was wrong about who met it ; con: the plan then records a lane that was never needed, which is a small dishonesty unless the reason is written beside it
| respec-to-the-real-gap — rewrite the exit around the two routes that genuinely do not exist: an invitation **list** and a **revoke** — pro: it points the lane at the only unbuilt thing, and a manager currently cannot see whether a code is live or withdraw one sent to the wrong person ; con: that is backend work in a lane classed and briefed as frontend, so it is a different lane wearing this one's name
| split — close this lane as built and author the list/revoke lane separately — pro: each record then says something true, and the backend work gets a brief written for backend work ; con: two entries where the plan had one, for a gap that is currently one route pair
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: a pilot manager demonstrably needs list and revoke this week, which raises the successor lane rather than reopening the close
ruled: split 2026-08-05 by @sven

**Whichever is ruled, one thing must not be "fixed" later: two of the three refusals the brief asked for are
impossible by design, and that is a security property rather than a shortfall.** Invalid, expired, revoked,
already-claimed, wrong-recipient and archived-person **all collapse to an identical
`404 workforce.invitation-invalid`** with no discriminating extension — an explicit anti-oracle, pinned at
`WorkforceInvitationTests.cs:493` (`Invalid_expired_and_used_tokens_are_indistinguishable_anti_oracle`,
verified present at `8e2b57de`). **The existing UI naming all five causes and picking none is the correct
design.** A future lane that "improves" this by surfacing a reason would break a pinned control, and my
brief asked for exactly that improvement.

**The lane also corrected itself on the record**, which is why its account is trustworthy: it had earlier
called those refusals a small follow-up, then read the backend and withdrew that.

**The honest cost it attached to its own green:** the walk is **fixture-backed**. On a real API,
`lane/wf-bootstrap` is still required — every workforce write needs a capability, a capability needs an
existing engagement, and **no endpoint mints the first one**, so a store with zero engagements has no way in
but a SQL insert. The fixture seeds the manager directly. **The surface is proven; the cold-start path to it
is not**, and that belongs to the bootstrap lane.

The invite surface, its routes, its nav entries and a committed green browser journey capturing manager-issues → worker-claims → worker-sees-own-schedule ALL already exist at baseline e34977ac (landed by 35440cf), so this lane's exit criterion is satisfied before it starts and there is nothing left to build.





### Decision D-EV-INQUIRY-UNGATED — whether a guest may raise an enquiry for a store that has not opened Events
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: F-EV-INQUIRY-UNGATED
options:
| refuse-the-write — gate the public enquiry write on the store's Events core flag — pro: no guest ever receives a confirmation for a booking the venue cannot see, which is the concrete harm today ; con: it may close the front door on the thing that sells the module, since the enquiry form is plausibly how a venue discovers Events at all
| unreachable-not-refused — leave the write ungated but stop the form being reachable for an un-opted store — pro: the same harm is prevented without a refusal a guest experiences as a fault, and an un-opted venue simply has no public surface ; con: reachability is a weaker guarantee than a gate — a stale link, a cached page or a direct POST still writes, so the harm returns by a quieter route
| deliberate-and-recorded — keep it open, and record in the plan that an enquiry for an un-opted store is intentional lead capture — pro: it is honest about what the form is for, and costs nothing to implement ; con: somebody must then own what happens to those rows, because today they are a confirmation to a guest and silence at the venue
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: a product decision gives enquiries from un-opted stores a real owner, such as routing them to sales
ruled: refuse-the-write 2026-08-05 by @sven

**Raised because the flag it answers says outright that this is a product call, not a defect.** The lane
that gated accept and decline **deliberately left the public enquiry write alone** and said why — which was
the right call and is why there is a decision here rather than a fix.

**The harm as it stands:** a guest can create an event row for a store whose admin surface answers **404** —
**a confirmation for a booking the venue can never see.**

**The reason it is not simply a bug:** the enquiry form is plausibly how a venue discovers the module at
all, so refusing the write may close the front door on the thing that sells it.

**One thing already settled and not in question**, recorded so no option quietly reopens it: the same lane
**left the payment callback ungated on purpose**, because gating it would strand in-flight money, and that
posture is already documented against the deposits surface. Whichever option is ruled here, it does not
extend to the callback.

**Fable recommends `refuse-the-write` — and both halves are already built and idle.** A backend lane
implements exactly this option with a deliberately **uniform** refusal, so that one anonymous
sequential-id endpoint cannot be walked to enumerate which venues run Events, with 193 lines of gate tests; a
frontend lane withdraws the form on a standing refusal while surviving per-attempt ones.

**The lead-capture argument fails on the measured state.** Today's rows are a confirmation shown to the guest
and **silence at the venue** — nobody reads them, **so nothing is being captured.** Ruling this option means
adopting the built pair through the review protocol, not commissioning work.

### Decision D-SPEC-L-POS-TENDER-WIRE-REBASE — the plan contradicts what L-POS-TENDER-WIRE-REBASE observed
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-POS-TENDER-WIRE-REBASE
options:
ruled: drop 2026-08-05 by @sven
| drop — strike the lane and record the branch as contained, which is what the census already says
|   pro: it is exactly what was measured; 0 ahead of the tip, 61 behind, and compose.md:447 already files it under "Contained — merge is a no-op, do not merge". Costs nothing and removes a merge-order hazard that no longer exists.
|   con: the lane also carried the only pointer in this plan at an unwalked money journey. Strike it and nobody owns the fact that no person has made a credit sale at a till.
| respec-journey — keep the lane and rewrite its exit around the half that is still open: a person completes a credit sale at a till
|   pro: C5 is standing law and this is the clearest live instance of it. The code is proven by mutation in both drift directions and is DI-registered; what is missing is a person, which is the gate.
|   con: it is a different class of work from the one granted, on a tier this lane was not resourced for, and re-pointing an exit breaks the joins the ledger and the runs/ records use.
| respec-deadguard — rewrite the exit around the new finding: the RETREC guard at KassaCreditSale.cs:28 reds nothing
|   pro: measured, cheap, and non-vacuous by construction — the same run's M4 control proves that scope does exercise the predicate, so this is a dead branch and not an unexercised one.
|   con: it is a defensive guard on a money path and the SQL tier never ran. Deleting code because a green suite does not miss it is the shape that has already cost this program twice.

**The lane measured its own premise before acting on it, which is why this is a clean refutation rather
than a disagreement.** It did not stop at the branch topology. It counted **definitions rather than files**
as instructed, and found the seventh twin real at `32fd5a86` — `FinalizeService.cs:237` classifying off the
request payment list — and **already consolidated at the tip** to a single
`KassaCreditSale.IsCreditSale(JournalEntry)` with six call sites, by `3a509b68` and `1854f594`.

**The clerk's "two other lanes still carry the private predicate" was wrong by roughly sixty-five times, and
the lane then showed the count was the wrong question.** About 130 live branches still contain the old
predicate in their trees. Rather than report that number, it **simulated every outstanding merge and counted
definitions in the result**: 111 of 111 yield exactly one, none yield two, because git takes the tip's
deletion where no branch modified that file. **A file-keyed count would have raised a false alarm on 130
branches.**

**The classification proof needed two mutations, and one would have been a false green.** Classifying off
the request reds the mirror-drift arm; gating the handover on the request reds the forward-drift arm.
**Neither mutation reds both**, so two distinct mechanisms hold the two directions and a single proof would
have passed while covering half the behaviour.

**It also caught the stale-build trap** this repository's own instructions document: a `--no-build` run
measured a binary still carrying a previous mutant. Every figure above comes from a run verified to have
compiled, by assembly timestamp.

**What is not closed.** C5 is untouched — **no person has walked the till credit-sale journey**; every
result here is a suite fact. That is the substance behind the second option.

default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: the plan turns out to have no mechanism carrying a dropped lane's survivors, in which case the unwalked money journey loses its only pointer

The brief orders a rebase of lane/meals-pos-tender-wire onto the integration tip, but that branch is already an ancestor of 8e2b57de (61 behind, 0 ahead) so there is nothing to rebase and nothing to land.




**Fable recommends `drop` — the premise is dead — but insists the drop must not be silent.** The lane it was
to rebase is **already an ancestor of the tip**, 0 ahead and 61 behind, so there is nothing to rebase.

**Two survivors must be re-homed in the same ruling.** A C5 item for the **unwalked till credit-sale
journey**, because a person and not a suite is the gate; and a flag on the RETREC guard, **explicitly barred
from deletion on suite-green alone while the SQL tier has not run** — deleting a money-path guard on a green
suite is the shape that has already cost this program twice.

### Decision D-REBASE-CONFLICTING-HEADS — 28 of 61 frontend heads will not merge, and 16 conflict with the tip itself
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-COMPOSE-FE-CANDIDATE
options:
| authors-rebase — one lane per conflicting head, each rebasing its own branch onto e34977ac
|   pro: whoever rebases a branch should know what it meant. Each head is re-proved at a tip that exists, and a bad resolution is contained to one lane and one reviewer.
|   con: those authors' sessions have ended, so "the author" is a new agent reading someone else's diff. It is sixteen lanes, and this program has sixteen lanes of higher-value work queued behind them.
| one-rebase-lane — a single lane rebases all sixteen mechanically onto the tip
|   pro: one act, one reviewer, one place to look when it goes wrong. Ordering ceases to matter once every head descends from the same commit.
|   con: one agent resolving sixteen unfamiliar conflicts is precisely what the composition brief forbids — "a candidate that got eleven steps in with a named blocker is worth far more than one that got sixty-one in by resolving conflicts on judgement".
| land-the-clean-thirty-five-first — land what already merges, then re-cut the sixteen from the new tip
|   pro: two thirds of the value lands now, and some of the sixteen may stop conflicting once the tip carries the work they were written beside. It shrinks the problem before anyone resolves anything.
|   con: it moves our branch before the journey tier is green, and the standing instruction was to prove everything on the candidate before merging into anything else.
| drop-and-reauthor — abandon the sixteen branches and rebuild their work against the current tip
|   pro: no conflict resolution at all. Each lane re-proves its own exit against a tip that exists, which is the only thing that has reliably worked here.
|   con: it discards work that was built and in some cases reviewed, and it repeats effort that a rebase would have preserved.
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: the Meals and Growth backend halves cannot land promptly, in which case landing the candidate ships two broken surfaces and the unstage questions reopen
ruled: land-the-clean-thirty-five-first 2026-08-05 by @sven

**Raised by `L-COMPOSE-FE-CANDIDATE`, and it is the finding that outranks the candidate it was asked to
build.** The census at §7 declined to ask whether the heads merge. The composition lane asked: **28 of 61 do
not, and 16 of those conflict with the pristine tip `e34977ac` itself.** For those sixteen, **no ordering
strategy composes them** — the twelve others are genuinely order-sensitive and are a scheduling problem, but
these are not. They need rebases nobody has scheduled, and the lane may not rewrite other lanes' branches.

**What was built while the question was open, so this is not a stall.** `candidate/fe-compose-2026-08-05`
carries **35 of 64 heads** at `9f7d8df` with jest green — 126 suites, 2959 tests. Nothing was forced; every
conflict was aborted rather than resolved.

**And the candidate is not clean, which is why the lane returned `blocked` rather than `built`.** The browser
journey tier reds **8 of 29 against 2 of 22 at the tip** — one genuine regression in `meals-admin-setup`,
which passes at the tip, plus six new journeys that fail on arrival including the § 8-5-6 kodeoversikt
download. **A green suite over seven journeys that do not complete is this estate's signature failure**, and
stopping there was the instruction.

**The lane corrected three of its own errors rather than burying them, and one changed its result.** It read
`jest.config.js` from the dirty shared checkout and took it for the tip's truth, so its first run measured the
wrong suite for 62 steps; redone, and the first run preserved unedited. That correction **recovered** a head
it had excluded as red, because the red was its own collector. It then reconciled the twin pair — having first
proved no landed head had touched those four files — and made a falsifiable prediction: that
`lane/L-PRICE-SHADOW-GUARD` would then merge green. **It did, as the thirty-fifth head, proving both
`shadows == []` and `PINNED_SHADOWS == []`.**



**One head's blocker is closed, measured on the candidate itself, 2026-08-05.** `L-MEALS-ENROL-JOURNEY-LOCATOR`
fixed the strict-mode collision at `d320105` and then cherry-picked it onto candidate tip `9f7d8df` in a
detached worktree: **the `meals-admin-setup` walk completes end to end across all 35 landed heads.** Line 131 was
that journey's only blocker. The candidate branch itself was not moved.

**And the ruling went against the spec rather than the product**, which matters for how the remaining
conflicts should be read. `.meals-programs .mls-note--warn` named a class every warning in the enrolment panel
carries while meaning one sentence. The counterfactual settles it: **only two of the four matches are gated on
the unread membership, so even had the read answered, the selector would still have matched two.** It could
never have resolved to one element again. The panel is not over-warning — each of its three notes says
something distinct and true.


**The candidate's journey tier is clean, measured on isolated ports with every run's fixture identified by pid,
cwd and self-reported port, 2026-08-05.**

| ref | journeys | passed | failed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| tip `e34977ac` | 22 | 21 | 1 — `workforce-schedule-publish`, an `@live` failure |
| candidate `9f7d8df` | 29 | 27 | 2 — the above, plus `meals-admin-setup` |

**The entire difference between the endpoints is one journey**, already attributed to `55b2dcd` and already
fixed on a lane branch. The triage tier reproduced its exact four-element strict-mode violation independently,
which corroborates the bisect rather than repeating it.

**So the class this triage was authored to populate is empty: zero real regressions on arrival, zero walks that
never passed, six harness-shape failures.** Every one of the six was the foreign-fixture defect or the
hardcoded-port defect inside it.

**Two further claims from the composition run fall with it.** `account-email-confirm` **passes at the tip**, so
"the composition fixed it" was never true — the tip row was poisoned by the same fixture. And the § 8-5-6
kodeoversikt walk **downloads its file, the template carries the right codes, and two clicks append two
actor-stamped issue rows** — the statutory failure reported three times to Sven did not exist.

**What was deliberately not done, and said rather than buried:** no origin-branch runs, on the ground that a
candidate PASS refutes both classes and all six spec blobs are byte-identical between origin and candidate.


**The manifest is in, 433 refs classified — frontend 116, backend 317 — and it changes what this decision is
about.** Containment was tested with `merge-base --is-ancestor` by object and then **re-tested at content level
with `git cherry`**, which is what caught the cases ancestry alone gets wrong.

**Five branches this plan may still think are pending are in the candidate**, and three more are
commit-absent but **content already applied**. The inverse trap is `c4a4fa44`: **an ancestor of nothing, yet 10
of its 11 files are already in the candidate by hand reconciliation** — trial-merged to confirm it does not
reintroduce the `priceLabel` money-gate shadow.

**Forty-five frontend branches carry a real unlanded fix, and the money work is one head, not six.** The chain
is six deep; **merging `c32cda3c` lands all of it**, and a peer list would have merged the same work three
times. **That merge conflicts, on `XReportView.vue` and `utils/price.js` — both money-path.** Of 25 heads
trial-merged, **19 conflict and 4 are clean.**

**The four-way question in this lane's exit collapses to three on the frontend**, because
`feature/restaurant-modules` is a strict ancestor of the candidate — *in modules only* is empty **by
construction, not by omission.**

**And `integration/mig-stack-land` is a fork rather than a superset** — 34 ahead, 59 behind, carrying **seven
migrations the integration branch lacks.** C2 is open whichever of the two is treated as the chain, and the
lane that recorded the stacking only records it.

**Not classified, and said so:** 136 backend branches with tips dated 2026-08-03 or earlier are listed with
containment but not described, because **patch-id is not conclusive in an estate that rebases before landing** —
which the duplicate CORS commit proves.


**Reviewed, and the review changed the number this decision turns on.** Every ancestry and containment claim in
the manifest was re-derived by object and **held**; the errors are in the counts, and one of them **understates
the work in the direction that would mislead this ruling.**

**The conflict census is not 19 of 25. It is 26 of 30.** The summary sentence miscounted by one, omitted a head
listed *not run* while keeping it in the denominator — it conflicts on 8 files — and **five older-lane heads
were never trial-merged at all. All five conflict, 10 to 13 files each.** Only four heads merge clean. **A
landing plan sized on 19 is undersized by seven authored merges.**

**The money-chain claim is the strongest part of the document and survives intact.** All five pairwise ancestry
links hold, each of the six commits has exactly one parent, and `rev-list` counts exactly six over the modules
tip. **"Merging the head lands all six" is true for any completed merge, not only a fast-forward** — with
author resolution confined to the two money-path files the manifest names, re-measured exact. **And the reason
a peer list would triple-merge is now precise: the three deepest commits each exist under two ref names,
byte-identical aliases in different namespaces.**

**The `priceLabel` shadow claim was verified more strongly than it was made.** The reviewer extracted the actual
merged tree: the merged `CustomerInfoModal.vue` blob is **byte-identical to the candidate's**, and the invoice
page declares no local `priceLabel` on either side. **Measured, not narrated.**

**The patch-id caveat is asymmetric, which rescues eight claims.** Rebase-blindness breaks only the *negative*
direction — a `+` does not prove absence — while a `-` is **positive evidence** an equivalent diff is already in
the target. All eight content-equivalence claims stand on that, and five of them rest on object ancestry where
patch-id plays no part at all.

**"Forty-five carry a real unlanded fix" is 43, or 44 if a comment correction counts.** One branch's entire
payload is a single evidence file — which the manifest's own table admits while still counting it — and
another's only non-evidence change is comment-only. **The exclusion rule was applied to one branch and not the
other.**

**Seven frontend heads created since the census cut are unclassified**, all of them lanes dispatched tonight.
**The ruling must either classify them or state the cutoff explicitly.** The backend census has **zero ref
drift**.


**All seven conditions applied, none refused, each re-measured by object before being written in — and the
re-measurement added three things the review had not found.**

**The old figure failed on its own arithmetic.** "19 of 25 conflict, 4 clean" does not add up, and nobody
caught it until somebody re-ran the merges. The corrected census is **26 of 30 conflict, 4 clean**: the 24
recorded verdicts are 20 conflicts not 19, one head sat in the denominator while listed *not run* and conflicts
on 8 files, and **the five older heads were never trial-merged at all — they conflict on 10, 10, 11, 13 and 11
files.** **A landing plan sized on 19 is short by seven authored merges.** One of the four clean heads turns out
to be a **fast-forward**: its parent is the candidate tip.

**The CORS commit is not a bad commit — it is a stale resolution, and that distinction changes the remedy.**
At its own base, `Program.cs` exposed exactly `"ETag"` and the constant that replaced it **did not yet exist**.
So the older commit **was correct where it was written** and is wrong only as a resolution against today's tip.
The rule now written in: **merge both, resolve to the newer side, and check it with a download arriving under a
readable filename.**

**The false edge is confirmed and it hid two family members**, not just one relationship — the commit joins two
steps later than drawn, at a merge the diagram omits entirely, and the conclusion it supports survives
re-verification.

**And the sentence about test evidence was a half-quote.** It cited a lane's message while **that same message
records a mutation that does red** — so the claim was not merely inherited, it was inherited selectively. It now
carries its provenance.

**The frontend count moved inside the correcting lane's own pass** — the review named seven new heads, the lane
measured **eight at 04:12Z and nine at 04:21Z** — so the cut-off is now stated as a timestamp rather than
implied. Backend drift is **zero**, established by comparing sets rather than counting.

**The editing standard held:** 360 lines to 568, **nothing deleted**, every change marked with what it said
before, and the census's own stated limitations kept and extended by one.


**A premise of this ruling is now measured false, and the measurement was taken after the ruling.** The
rationale included that re-cutting the conflicting heads from a new tip "may shrink the problem". It does not.

**All 28 unlanded heads were re-tested against the composed candidate with a dry merge, nothing merged: zero
became clean, and for eleven of them the conflicted surface grew** — one from 23 files to 28, another from 10
to 13, another from 14 to 16.

**The sharper half is what it means for scheduling the re-cut.** The twelve order-induced heads conflict on
**zero** files against the pristine tip — each merges clean onto it alone — and on one to three files each
against the candidate. **Landing the clean thirty-five is what costs them their clean merge.**

**The ruling stands as ruled; this is recorded beside it rather than over it.** What changes is the
expectation: whoever schedules the re-cut should plan for it being **marginally harder than before, not
easier**, and the order-induced twelve are cheapest taken from the tip rather than from the composition.

### Decision D-MIG21-WHICH-TRIGGER-WINS — two migration files claim MIG-21 and the second one to run fails hard
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-MIG-STACK-RECORD
options:
| keep-23f6bbeb — land the later file and drop `a6a1174b`'s from the stack
|   pro: it is the one on the chain the other thirteen stacked branches descend from, so keeping it leaves the ten-link chain intact and touches nothing else.
|   con: it drops a commit off `lane/margin-finalize-lag` that its author has not been asked about, and that branch may carry other work that assumes its own file is present.
| keep-a6a1174b — land the earlier file and drop the other
|   pro: it is the original; the later one is the duplicate that appeared afterwards.
|   con: it is off-chain, so keeping it means renumbering or re-parenting the chain that already descends from the other — the expensive direction.
| guard-both — add `IF OBJECT_ID` guards so either order is survivable, and land both
|   pro: it removes the hard failure without anybody having to choose whose commit dies, and a guarded trigger creation is defensible on its own terms.
|   con: it leaves two migrations claiming one number, which is the condition that produced this, and a guard that makes a collision survivable makes the next one silent.
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: a commit appears on the losing lane beyond its current tip that depends on the dropped migration id — none exists today
ruled: keep-23f6bbeb 2026-08-05 by @sven

**This is the only case in the estate where two real migration files claim one number**, found by a census of 28
numbers across 317 backend heads. `a6a1174b` / `20260731203011` against `23f6bbeb` / `20260801102621`, **neither
an ancestor of the other.**

**The two files differ by an eight-line comment.** Same `CREATE TRIGGER`, same `THROW 50060` and `50061`. It
would be tempting to call that harmless.

**It is not, because neither carries an `IF OBJECT_ID` guard.** Landing both does not apply the same DDL twice
to no effect — **the second `Up()` fails hard**, on whichever database replays the chain, which is a fresh
database and never the author's.

**Why it needs a person.** Every option deletes somebody's commit or changes a shape nobody agreed to. The
clerk may not drop a lane's work, and the third option trades a loud failure for a quiet one, which is a
judgement about what this estate wants to be told.



**Fable recommends `keep-23f6bbeb`, and the con protecting the other side is measured false.** The lane whose
id would be dropped is **exactly one commit ahead** of its merge-base, and that commit's entire payload — same
nine files, same tests, trigger body verbatim — **was already regenerated on the chain tip**, by a commit
whose own migration file documents the supersession: the lane's id would have forked the Designer parent and
broken fresh replays. **Nothing of the author's work dies except the stale id.**

**`guard-both` is the C1-hostile option**: it trades a loud failure for a silent one **on the fiscal-trigger
chain where this estate already shipped RF-1313.**

**One nit for the record:** this block's prose names a different migration file than the one that is actually
duplicated in that tree. **The ruling resolves the same way**, but the citation is wrong.

### Decision D-MEALS-MEMBERS-READ-LANDING — the dangerous half is already composed, and not deciding chooses it
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-MEALS-MEMBERS-READ-LAND-CHECK
options:
| land-both — merge backend `lane/meals-members-read` and keep the frontend half in the composition
|   pro: it is the only combination in which what the manager reads is true. The backend half is 1 ahead and 0 behind — a clean fast-forward — and the frontend half is already merged into the candidate, so this is the smaller of the two remaining acts.
|   con: it is a cross-repo landing on a shared branch, which is yours; and the backend half has not been reviewed.
| unstage-the-frontend — take `2e3f39d` back out of the composition candidate and land neither for now
|   pro: it restores the only other honest world. With neither half, there is no enrolment section at all, and nothing on screen claims one exists — the manager is not told anything false.
|   con: it removes a built and mutation-proved capability from a candidate that took 35 merges to assemble, and it must be redone later anyway.
| land-frontend-only, deliberately — accept the composed state and record why
|   pro: nothing else in the candidate has to move, and the panel's data half works: the programmes table fills with real Company Meals data.
|   con: this is the state described below, in which the product tells a manager to reload forever for a route that will never exist. Choosing it deliberately at least puts the cost on the record instead of leaving it to a default.
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: the review of the single backend commit finds something, in which case unstage temporarily rather than let the composed state reach the shared branch
ruled: land-both 2026-08-05 by @sven

**A real pair, unlike the two asserted earlier tonight, and measured rather than assumed.** Backend
`lane/meals-members-read` at `086ac34f` is 1 ahead and 0 behind — a clean fast-forward. The frontend half at
`9fbed80` is 4 ahead and 2 behind. `ListProgramMembersAsync` lives on exactly one api ref.

**The four combinations collapse to three, and on the opposite axis from the one the clerk guessed.** *Neither*
and *backend alone* are the same world, not *neither* and *frontend alone*: the enrolment control **arrives
entirely with the frontend half**, so the integration branch has **zero** enrolment hooks against eight on both
frontend refs. Backend alone is a dead route and an error code no web ref renders — invisible and harmless.

**Frontend alone is the dangerous world, and it does not look broken.** Twelve of thirteen routes exist, so the
programmes table fills with real data. Beneath it the manager reads *"Tick everybody who should be enrolled"* —
unconditional, no `v-if` — above boxes that are not there; *"Reload and try again"* for a route that will never
exist; and *"This server did not answer as Company Meals. We do not know whether the module is here."* **They
are told the module may not be installed while looking at its data, and they reload forever.** Not a data-loss
risk; the control is genuinely withheld.

**The note was replaced, not deleted, and that is worse.** `meals_enrol_no_read_note` became
`meals_enrol_unread_note` — **a permanent absence wearing a transient face, with a retry instruction attached.**

**Not deciding decides.** `2e3f39d` is already merged into `candidate/fe-compose-2026-08-05`; the api half is
merged nowhere. **The composed state is the dangerous one.**

**And no guard catches it.** The members read is deliberately unanchored in the divergence check, and the
journey's fixture defaults to answering a route the merge candidate lacks. **Green in CI, self-contradicting on
screen.**

**Symmetry with the workforce invite pair: inverted.** That pair's quiet half is *frontend* alone; this pair's
quiet half is *backend* alone. Each pair's dangerous direction is the other's safe one — **and this one's
dangerous direction is the one already composed.**


**One refinement from the branch manifest, which traced the failure rather than assuming it.** The panel maps
the missing GET to `DATA_UNKNOWN` and **withholds the enrol control** — so on the data side that direction is
**loud and safe**, not silent. That agrees with this decision's own measurement, which says the control is
genuinely withheld and no data is at risk.

**The two readings differ only in what "dangerous" names.** The manifest is describing the data path; this
decision is describing what a manager reads — *"Tick everybody who should be enrolled"* above absent boxes, and
a retry instruction for a route that will never exist. **Both are true: the control is safe and the copy is
misleading**, and it is the copy that costs an operator their morning.


### Decision D-GR-WITHDRAW-PAIR — a third pair, and the shipped half is the loud one
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-FIX-BRANCH-MANIFEST
options:
| land-the-backend-halves — merge the two backend halves so the frontend already in the candidate has something to talk to
|   pro: it is the only combination where consent withdrawal works. Both authors independently wrote that shipping one half alone leaves the page exactly as broken, which is unusual agreement between lanes that never spoke.
|   con: it is a cross-repo landing on a shared branch, and it carries the duplicate-CORS hazard below, so it cannot be done by merging every branch that touches the policy.
| unstage-the-frontend — take the two frontend halves back out of the candidate
|   pro: restores a coherent world where the withdrawal page is absent rather than silently refused.
|   con: removes work already composed, and must be redone.
| land-nothing-yet — accept the composed state and record it
|   pro: nothing has to move while the other five decisions are open.
|   con: the composed state is a consent-withdrawal path that refuses **with no status code, no server log line and no rendered refusal** — and no test reds either way.
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: the withdrawal page turns out to be feature-hideable in the candidate more cheaply than the backend halves can land
ruled: land-the-backend-halves 2026-08-05 by @sven

**Found by the branch manifest as the third must-land-together pair, and it is the worst-shaped of the three.**
`fe-gr-withdraw-origin` and `fe-growth-prefcentre` are **in the candidate**; the backend halves are **in neither
anchor**.

**The backend is the quiet half, which inverts the other two pairs.** Without it the failure is a
**credentialed-CORS preflight refusal** — no status code, no server log line, no rendered refusal, **on a
consent-withdrawal path**, and **no test reds either way**. A person clicks withdraw and nothing happens.

**Both authors independently reached the same conclusion**, in lanes that never communicated: shipping one half
alone leaves the page exactly as broken.

**And it carries a duplicate-fix hazard that a merge would not surface.** The CORS policy exists as **two
commits with an identical subject and distinct patch-ids** — `2a052800` (2026-08-03 11:22) and its rebase
`3c71b323` (2026-08-04 20:24). The clerk verified both. **Merging `lane/cors-followups` and
`lane/gr-withdraw-origin` lands the same change twice.** The manifest's recommendation is to take
`cors-followups` and drop the other four for that change — **a de-duplication by timestamp would not have found
it**, since the timestamps differ by a day while the subjects match exactly.

**The duplicate is not a duplicate, and that turns the dedup advice into a correctness requirement.** The
clerk verified both lines: `2a052800` writes `.WithExposedHeaders("ETag")`; `3c71b323` writes
`.WithExposedHeaders(BrowserReadableHeaders.All)`, **and its own doc-comment records that the hardcoded literal
silently dropped `Content-Disposition` and `X-Meals-Content-Hash`.**

**So the earlier commit is not merely redundant — it is wrong**, and the manifest's advice to *"take
`cors-followups` and drop the other four"* **cannot be followed as written**, because `lane/gr-withdraw-origin`
carries `2a052800` and **is this pair's backend half.** It cannot be dropped.

**The resolution rule, therefore:** when both land, `Helpers/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs` must resolve to
`3c71b323`'s side — **never the hardcoded literal.** A merge that takes the older side restores a header
suppression nobody would see, on the paths that download documents.


**Fable's cross-cutting finding, 2026-08-05: the three landing pairs are one shape and must not get one
ruling, because their dangerous directions differ.** Two of the three frontend halves are **already composed
into the candidate**; the third is not.

**Meals and Growth therefore gate the candidate landing.** Their frontend halves are in the composition, so
their backend halves must be on the backend tip **before or with** the candidate, or landing ships a
self-contradicting Meals panel and a **silent consent-withdrawal refusal** — no status code, no log line, no
rendered refusal, no red test — onto the shared branch. **In both, not deciding chooses the harmful world.**

**The invite pair is the opposite case and the only one that genuinely needs a review first.** Its frontend
half is **not** composed, so nothing dangerous is live, and it is the largest unreviewed diff in the program —
23 files, roughly 1,700 lines — and it inverts two pins. There is no urgency to justify landing that unread.

**One resolution rule must be pinned wherever the Growth halves land:** the shared service-collection file
resolves to the newer commit's header allowlist, **never** the older literal — the older one silently drops
two headers, so it is wrong rather than merely duplicate.

### Decision D-SPEC-L-ARM-RECEIPTS-RECAPTURE — the plan contradicts what L-ARM-RECEIPTS-RECAPTURE observed
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-ARM-RECEIPTS-RECAPTURE
options:
ruled: respec-per-backend 2026-08-05 by @sven
| accept-as-built — treat the clause as satisfied by backendBuild for live-backed receipts and close the lane
|   pro: the design is deliberate and documented at journey.js:657 — a live API's working directory is not this checkout, so identity for live worlds is backendBuild's job, and backendBuild is exactly what caught the two arm-3 originals naming a build nobody can check out.
|   con: it leaves two different provenance contracts in the plan, and the next lane reading the exit will have to rediscover which family it is in.
| respec-per-backend — rewrite the exit so a receipt names its fixture when fixture-backed and its backendBuild when live-backed
|   pro: it states the real contract instead of one family's version of it, and it is what the clerk should have written; the census's five re-runs were all fixture-backed and the clause was generalised from them.
|   con: re-pointing an exit breaks the joins the ledger and the runs/ records use, and the lane has already done the work either way.
| extend-the-harness — make servingFixture resolve for live backends too, then re-capture
|   pro: one provenance field for every receipt, and no reader has to know which family they are looking at.
|   con: it means editing the journey.js whose sha both provers testify to, which invalidates the ten captures just taken and every green measured against that ref. The lane refused to do this unasked, correctly.

**The lane ruled rather than improvised, and its reading is right.** `journey.js:657` resolves `servingFixture`
**only when `backend === "fixture"`**, with a documented rationale: a live API's working directory is not this
checkout by design, so identity for live worlds belongs to `backendBuild`. **All ten arm-N receipts are
`backend: "live"` by arm assertion**, and the stand-in API 404s the health endpoint on purpose — measured
`identitySource: "none"` on all ten.

**The clause is the clerk's error, and its origin is specific.** It was generalised from the artifacts census's
five re-runs, **which were all fixture-backed.** It does not survive contact with this receipt family.

**Three of the four exit clauses are met and the ten receipts exist**, taken from a clean worktree detached at
`7030c00` with `porcelain` empty before and after every run, both provers re-measured by the lane itself —
10 of 10 and 5 of 5, twice — each printing the ref's own `journey.js` sha and a build id with no `+dirty`.

**The first pass did print `+dirty`, and the instrument caught its own operator.** Two untracked run logs
written *inside* the worktree were enough. **That is a live hazard for any lane filing evidence into the
checkout it measures**, and it is the reason this one's output was moved out and the run repeated.

**What the re-capture found is the substance, and it is the first direct evidence of what the dead guard let
through.** Ten of ten differ, and two differences are real:

- **Both arm-3 originals name a build nobody can check out** — `Web-modules@…+dirty`, twice. The prefix is the
  port holder's directory basename, so **both were captured from the shared main checkout, dirty.**
- **Five receipts carry fields that exist in `journey.js` at none of the relevant refs.** Their sole producer is
  a commit on a lane branch that is **not an ancestor** of the ref they were committed to. **They were captured
  by a harness that is not on the branch they were filed into, by a tree that cannot emit their fields.**

**And the reassuring half, which matters as much:** the probe substance is **identical across all ten pairs** —
status, backend, surface, capabilities, findings, error and all three served-counters. **Only provenance moved.**
The captures were right and unwitnessed, exactly as the census framed it.

default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: the ledger and per-backend run joins demonstrably cannot survive an exit re-word

journey.js:657 resolves servingFixture only when backend=="fixture"; all ten arm-N receipts are backend=="live" by arm assertion, so "each carrying servingFixture resolved to this run's own fixture" is unmeetable at 7030c00 without editing the journey.js sha both provers testify to.




**Fable recommends `respec-per-backend`.** At the receipts' own ref the harness resolves the serving fixture
**only when the backend is the fixture**, with the live-world rationale written in place — identity for a live
world belongs to the build stamp. **So the clause is unmeetable as written**, and accepting as built would
leave an exit in the plan that **no live-backed receipt can ever satisfy**: a written expectation that gates
nothing, this set's defect in prose form.

**Extending the harness instead would invalidate the ten recaptured receipts** and every green measured
against the sha both provers testify to. The work is done; only the wording is wrong.

### Decision D-HUSKY-HOOKS-ESTATE-WIDE — seventeen dead hooks in one directory behind ninety worktrees
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-LINT-RUNNABLE
options:
| remove — delete the hooks from the shared common directory
|   pro: they do nothing today and they look like enforcement to anyone reading the tree, which is worse than no hooks. They were installed by one lane's `npm install` rather than by anybody's decision.
|   con: deleting shared state that ninety worktrees see is irreversible from any single lane's position, and if anyone is relying on a hook that does work, it goes with them.
| repair — make them fire, so the configured lint-staged runs
|   pro: it is what somebody once intended; `lint-staged` is configured and the rules are already at error.
|   con: **it arms a lint gate across the entire estate on the strength of one lane's dependency install** — and the repository currently reports 678 errors, so every commit anywhere would start failing at once.
| leave-and-record — keep them and write down that they are inert
|   pro: no shared state changes while eight other decisions are open, and the misleading appearance is at least documented.
|   con: the next person to read `.git/hooks` still believes there is a gate, which is the condition that produced this.
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: any branch is found whose package.json defines husky hooks — a search across all refs found only the initial commit
ruled: remove 2026-08-05 by @sven

**Not a lane's call, because the state is not a lane's.** The seventeen hooks sit in
`/Users/svendaneel/okam/Web/.git/hooks` — **the shared common directory behind roughly ninety worktrees**, 33
entries. A lane that repaired or removed them would change what every other worktree does.

**They are inert, proven by running one:** *"pre-commit config not found, skipping hook"*, exit 0. `hookIsDefined()`
greps for the hook's own name and finds nothing.

**And their provenance is the argument.** They were written by **one lane's `npm install`** on 2026-08-01, from
that lane's own `node_modules`. **Nobody decided to install them.**

**The repair option is the expensive one and its cost is measurable.** The repository reports **678 errors**
today across 172 of 607 files. Arming the gate turns every commit in every worktree red until those are fixed —
of which `curly`, `arrow-parens` and one Vue formatting rule are three quarters, and mostly auto-fixable.



**Fable recommends `remove`, having established the hooks are inert everywhere rather than merely unused
here.** 33 entries, husky v4 shims stamped from **a different repository's** node_modules — one lane's
accidental install — with **no `husky` key, no `.huskyrc`, and no branch in the estate's whole history that
ever configured hooks.** Removal therefore changes behaviour in no worktree, and the shims are two-line files
any reinstall recreates, so it is not irreversible either.

**Repair is the option that looks responsible and is not:** it would arm a gate nobody scheduled, on a tree
where three spot-checked files already carry 29 errors. **And leave-and-record keeps decoration that looks
like enforcement** — the precise defect this set indicts.

### Decision D-RECEIPT-MODAL-UNTESTABLE — a component no test can mount, and a template rewritten to change that
state: ruled
owner: @sven
blocks: L-GERMAN-IDENTIFIER-LABELS
options:
| accept-the-rewrite — keep the two template lines the lane changed and treat optional chaining as unavailable in this component
|   pro: it is the smallest change that makes the surface testable at all, and the surface is a receipt — the one artifact an inspector reads. Seven assertions now exist where none could.
|   con: a production template was changed to enable a test, which is an act this lane was not authorised for and which nobody reviewed as a product change.
| revert-and-lose-the-assertions — restore the template and accept that the receipt cannot be mounted
|   pro: no production line moves for a test's convenience, and the copy fix stands on its own.
|   con: the receipt modal then remains a surface **no test can mount at all**, which is how a mislabelled identifier survived on it in the first place.
| fix-the-toolchain — make the transform accept optional chaining, then revert the template
|   pro: it removes the constraint rather than working around it, and any other component with the same syntax becomes testable too.
|   con: it is a build-tooling change with an unmeasured blast radius across 878 files, and nothing in this repository currently runs a suite in CI to catch what it breaks.
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: a template-transpiler upgrade is measured green across the full suite, at which point revert the rewrite and take the toolchain
ruled: accept-the-rewrite 2026-08-05 by @sven

**Raised by the lane itself rather than absorbed, which is why it is here.** `components/molecules/ReceiptModal.vue`
**could not be mounted in jest at all** — the transform cannot parse optional chaining — so the lane rewrote
**two template lines** to make its seven assertions possible. All seven red when the German dictionary is
reverted.

**The act is the question, not the lines.** A copy-correction lane changed production markup to enable a test.
**That is a different kind of change from the one it was dispatched for**, and it should be ruled rather than
noticed later in a diff.

**And the surface is the reason it matters both ways.** A receipt is a kassasystemforskrifta artifact. **It is
also, until now, a surface no test could mount** — which is how a German label naming the wrong issuing
authority survived on it, one line above a second string naming the wrong register.

**Fable recommends `accept-the-rewrite`, and names what the ruling should open beside it.** The template
transpiler genuinely cannot parse optional chaining, the two-line rewrite is behaviour-identical for every
value the field can hold, and seven mounted assertions all red on a dictionary revert. **The surface is a
kassasystemforskrifta artifact that no test could mount — which is how a German authority label survived on
it.**

**Fixing the toolchain instead is an unmeasured change under 878 files with no CI suite to catch what it
breaks.** But per-component rewrites do not scale, and **three further unmountable templates are already
named**, so the recommendation is to ratify these two lines and open a separate toolchain lane for the rest.

### Decision D-SPEC-L-PAYMENTTYPE-COMPANYACCOUNT — the plan contradicts what L-PAYMENTTYPE-COMPANYACCOUNT observed

options:
ruled: drop-and-take-the-reachable-one 2026-08-05 by @sven
